title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
聖上德學日新勵精圖治思進天
下之多士丕乃俾乂爰納輔
臣之請以嘉靖戊子遣朝官
出各省主試事而世揚暨刑
部主事陳篪與主山東
命下兼程馳至乃八月七日甫入
===
敕院維巡按監察御史馬津
司監臨左布政使郭韶左叅
政邊憲司提調按察使顧應
祥副使成英司監試咸既厥
心教授劉詔學正羅釗教諭
胡浩王冕韓秉文趙時吉胡
文舉爲同考試官暨百執事
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

聖上德學日新，勵精圖治，思進天下之多士，丕乃俾乂。爰納輔臣之請，以嘉靖戊子遣朝官出各省主試事，而世揚暨刑部主事陳篪與主山東。命下，兼程馳至，乃八月七日甫入敕院。維巡按監察御史馬津司監臨，左布政使郭韶、左叅政邊憲司提調，按察使顧應祥、副使成英司監試，咸既厥心。教授劉詔、學正羅釗、教諭胡浩、王冕、韓秉文、趙時吉、胡文舉爲同考試官，暨百執事
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

His Majesty daily renews his virtue and learning, devotes himself diligently to good government, and seeks to advance the many scholars of the realm and thereby bring about great order. Accordingly, he accepted the request of his chief ministers and, in the wuzi year of Jiajing [1528], dispatched court officials to the provinces to preside over the examinations. I, Shiyang, together with Chen Chi, a Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, was assigned to preside jointly over the examination in Shandong. Once the command was issued, we hastened there by forced stages, entering the examination compound [?] only on the seventh day of the eighth month.

Ma Jin, Regional Inspector serving as an Investigating Censor, acted as Supervising Official. Guo Shao, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Bian Xian, Left Administration Vice Commissioner, acted as Proctors. Gu Yingxiang, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Cheng Ying, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, oversaw the conduct of the examination. All devoted themselves wholeheartedly to their duties. Liu Zhao, a Prefectural School Instructor; Luo Zhao, a Subprefectural School Instructor; and Hu Hao, Wang Mian, Han Bingwen, Zhao Shiji, and Hu Wenju, County School Instructors, served as Associate Examiners, together with all the other functionaries …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
分宅外内厰渠有恭乃合提
學副使余〔本暨副使劉淑相〕
遼東廵按御史王〔重賢〕所簡
士凡千八百人三試之舉其
賢者得七十五人校閱毋敢
不精去取毋敢不公所錄多
舉子本文或稍因脩飾潤畧
===
毋敢不實重得賢遵
詔旨也古者三年大比鄉老及
鄉大夫若州長興其土之賢
能則固其土之賢也是故知
素而擇精匪德行道藝弗興
焉今之校文與古殊邈所由
來遠矣亦有不得已焉耳夫
punctuated:
分宅外内，厰渠有恭。乃合提學副使余〔本暨副使劉淑相〕、遼東廵按御史王〔重賢〕所簡士，凡千八百人，三試之，舉其賢者，得七十五人。校閱毋敢不精，去取毋敢不公。所錄多舉子本文，或稍因脩飾潤畧，毋敢不實。重得賢，遵詔旨也。
古者三年大比，鄉老及鄉大夫若州長，興其土之賢能，則固其土之賢也。是故知素而擇精，匪德行道藝弗興焉。今之校文與古殊邈，所由來遠矣，亦有不得已焉耳。夫
translation_en:
…were assigned stations outside and within, and performed their duties respectfully [?; the transcription 厰渠 is unclear]. We then assembled the men selected by Yu Ben, Education Intendant and Vice Commissioner, together with Vice Commissioner Liu Shuxiang, and by Wang Chongxian, Regional Inspector of Liaodong: 1,800 men in all. We examined them in three sessions and selected the worthy among them, obtaining seventy-five men. In reviewing their papers, we dared be anything but meticulous; in rejecting or accepting them, we dared be anything but impartial. The writings recorded here are mostly the candidates’ original compositions. Where we made slight stylistic revisions, embellishments, or abridgments, we dared be anything but faithful to the originals. This was to give due weight to obtaining worthy men and to comply with the imperial edict.
In antiquity, at the great triennial assessment, the district elders, district grand masters, and subdistrict chiefs recommended the worthy and capable men of their own localities; these were indeed men of worth from those localities. Thus, knowing their usual conduct, they could select with discrimination; none were recommended unless they possessed virtuous conduct and proficiency in the Way and the arts. Today’s assessment of written compositions differs greatly from ancient practice. Its origins lie far in the past, and there are also circumstances that make it unavoidable. Now, …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
鳳麟出為世瑞而天下治其
羽毛章釆識者知焉謂鳳麟
專在於文不可也而知鳳麟
以文亦可也有不知者雖視
其文弗知其為鳳麟也山東
古大聖大賢之地士生其間
聞風嚮化超然遠詣固宜有
充實光輝敷賁詞章為世之
===
鳳麟者矣我
皇上明目達聰瑞在得賢嚴惟丕
式專事責成而世揚又非其
人誠懼斯地有鳳麟而弗知
又懼所知者非鳳麟也諸士
盍反而求之凡三試之文實
punctuated:
鳳麟出，為世瑞，而天下治。其羽毛章釆，識者知焉。謂鳳麟專在於文，不可也；而知鳳麟以文，亦可也。有不知者，雖視其文，弗知其為鳳麟也。山東，古大聖大賢之地，士生其間，聞風嚮化，超然遠詣，固宜有充實光輝、敷賁詞章，為世之鳳麟者矣。
我皇上明目達聰，瑞在得賢，嚴惟丕式，專事責成。而世揚又非其人，誠懼斯地有鳳麟而弗知，又懼所知者非鳳麟也。諸士盍反而求之？凡三試之文，實
translation_en:
… When phoenixes and qilin appear, they are auspicious signs for the age, and all under Heaven is well governed. Those with discernment recognize them by the splendid markings of their feathers and coats. To say that phoenixes and qilin consist solely in outward adornment would be wrong; yet to recognize them through that adornment is permissible. Those without discernment, even when they see those markings, do not know them to be phoenixes and qilin. Shandong is the land of the great sages and worthies of antiquity. Scholars born there hear of their example and respond to its transforming influence, rising above the ordinary and attaining lofty heights. Surely among them there should be those whose inner fullness and radiance find expression in literary composition, making them the phoenixes and qilin of their age.
Our Emperor sees clearly and hears widely, regarding the acquisition of worthy men as an auspicious sign. He solemnly upholds the grand rules [?] and makes it his particular concern to demand that entrusted duties be fulfilled. Yet I, Shiyang, am not equal to this charge. I truly fear that there are phoenixes and qilin in this land whom I fail to recognize; I also fear that those I recognize are not phoenixes and qilin. Why do you scholars not turn back and seek the answer within yourselves? As for the compositions of all three examination sessions, truly …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
得於讀書實踐於心身何如
學爲實學斯用爲實用則校
文之法雖令所不得已而與
者固古賢能也是故文以觀
學學以觀用文至而學未至
者亦有之矣未有學不至而
用至者也夫文一日也用終
身也一日者或可遇終身者
不可欺也不可欺而自欺則
===
一日之遇亦直欺耳
明天子經德秉哲迪知忱恂賢否
莫逃世揚將無稱匪其人之
懲乎夫人知主司之造士而
不知士之成主司也爾多士
punctuated:
得於讀書，實踐於心身何如？學爲實學，斯用爲實用，則校文之法，雖令所不得已，而與者固古賢能也。是故文以觀學，學以觀用。文至而學未至者，亦有之矣；未有學不至而用至者也。夫文，一日也；用，終身也。一日者或可遇，終身者不可欺也。不可欺而自欺，則一日之遇亦直欺耳。
明天子經德秉哲，迪知忱恂，賢否莫逃。世揚將無稱匪其人之懲乎？夫人知主司之造士，而不知士之成主司也。爾多士
translation_en:
…truly acquired through reading, and genuinely put into practice in your hearts and conduct—to what extent is this so? When learning is substantive learning, its application will be substantive application. Thus, although judging compositions is an unavoidable expedient at present [?], those admitted are indeed the worthy and capable men of antiquity. Hence compositions reveal learning, and learning reveals fitness for service. There are those whose compositions attain excellence while their learning does not; there has never been anyone whose learning falls short yet whose service attains excellence. Composition is a matter of one day; service is a matter of a lifetime. Success on a single day may come by chance, but a lifetime admits of no deception. If, where deception is impossible, one nevertheless deceives oneself, then even that single day's success is nothing but deception.
The enlightened Son of Heaven makes virtue his guiding principle and holds fast to wisdom; his understanding is truly profound, and neither worthiness nor unworthiness escapes him. Shall I, Shiyang, not incur punishment for recommending the wrong men? People know that the chief examiner nurtures scholars, but do not know that scholars establish the chief examiner's merit. You, the many scholars…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
其功以一日所得者自誦而
以終身所到者自力則以彼
之仁成此之明且交成事
上之忠一物而三善皆得者耶詩
曰王國克生維周之楨又曰
周王壽考遐不作人諸士其
生也有為其成也有賴將必
===
有深於學不欺於文為真才
為實用能為我宣厥猷者庶
無愧聖賢之地之士非〔世揚〕
之至願哉幸相與誠勗焉于
時都御史王〔堯封〕巡撫其地
綱紀一方巡鹽御史魏〔有本〕
右布政使戍〔文〕左叅政張〔宏〕
punctuated:
其功以一日所得者自誦，而以終身所到者自力，則以彼之仁成此之明，且交成事上之忠，一物而三善皆得者耶？《詩》曰：「王國克生，維周之楨。」又曰：「周王壽考，遐不作人。」諸士其生也有為，其成也有賴，將必有深於學、不欺於文、為真才、為實用、能為我宣厥猷者。庶無愧聖賢之地之士，非〔世揚〕之至願哉？幸相與誠勗焉。
于時，都御史王〔堯封〕巡撫其地，綱紀一方；巡鹽御史魏〔有本〕、右布政使戍〔文〕、左叅政張〔宏〕
translation_en:
…if [?] you recite to yourselves what you have gained in a single day, while exerting yourselves toward what you will attain over a lifetime, then their benevolence will fulfill our discernment, and together we will fulfill our loyalty in serving the sovereign. Would this not be to achieve all three virtues through one undertaking? The Book of Odes says: “The royal realm can bring forth men who are the pillars of Zhou.” It also says: “May the king of Zhou enjoy long life; does he not nurture men?” You scholars were born to accomplish something, and your fulfillment depends upon support. Surely among you there will be those whose learning is profound, whose writing is free of deception, who possess genuine ability and serve practical needs, and who can expound those counsels for us. May you thus prove worthy of being scholars from the land of sages and worthies. Is this not the deepest wish of Shiyang 世揚? I hope that we may sincerely encourage one another in this.
At this time, Censor-in-chief Wang Yaofeng 王堯封 served as Grand Coordinator of this territory, maintaining order throughout the region. Wei Youben 魏有本 was Salt-control Censor. Shu Wen 戍文 [?] was Right Provincial Administration Commissioner. Zhang Hong 張宏 was Left Administration Vice Commissioner …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
右叅政王〔潮〕左叅議鄺〔灝〕右
叅議何〔璦〕副使牛〔鸞〕葉〔溥〕陳
〔文沛〕聶〔珙〕僉事邊〔寧〕陳〔德鳴〕
謝〔旻〕王〔尚志〕沈〔圻〕都指揮盧
〔璽〕咸聳翊有勸宜書時則有
若勤百執事不能徧書披錄
可知已
===
徵仕郎戶科右給事中劉〔世〕
〔楊〕謹序
punctuated:
右叅政王〔潮〕、左叅議鄺〔灝〕、右叅議何〔璦〕、副使牛〔鸞〕、葉〔溥〕、陳〔文沛〕、聶〔珙〕、僉事邊〔寧〕、陳〔德鳴〕、謝〔旻〕、王〔尚志〕、沈〔圻〕、都指揮盧〔璽〕，咸聳翊有勸，宜書。時則有若勤百執事，不能徧書，披錄可知已。
徵仕郎戶科右給事中劉〔世〕〔楊〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Right Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Chao; Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Kuang Hao; Right Administration Assistant Commissioner He Ai; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Niu Luan, Ye Pu, Chen Wenpei, and Nie Gong; Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Bian Ning, Chen Deming, Xie Min, Wang Shangzhi, and Shen Qi; and Regional Military Commissioner Lu Xi all offered support and encouragement and deserve to be recorded. There were also the many officials who labored in their duties at this time [?]; they cannot all be recorded here, but their names may be learned by consulting this record.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Liu Shiyang, Gentleman for Service and Right Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue.

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖七年山東鄉試

巡按山東監察御史馬津〔宗孔直隸徐州人　丁丑進士〕
提調官
山東等處承宣布政使司左布政使郭韶〔克諧山西霍州人　乙未進士〕
山東等處承宣布政使司左參政邊憲〔汝明直隸任丘縣人　辛未進士〕

===

刑部雲南清吏司主事陳篪〔和韶福建莆田縣人　癸未進士〕

江西建昌府儒學教授劉詔〔汝承四川江津縣人　癸酉貢士〕

punctuated:
嘉靖七年山東鄉試

監臨官
巡按山東監察御史馬津〔宗孔，直隸徐州人，丁丑進士〕。

提調官
山東等處承宣布政使司左布政使郭韶〔克諧，山西霍州人，乙未進士〕。
山東等處承宣布政使司左參政邊憲〔汝明，直隸任丘縣人，辛未進士〕。

監試官
山東等處提刑按察司按察使顧應祥〔惟賢，浙江長興縣人，乙丑進士〕。
山東等處提刑按察司副使成英〔秀卿，順天府遵化縣人，戊辰進士〕。

考試官
戶科右給事中劉世揚〔實夫，福建閩縣人，丁丑進士〕。
刑部雲南清吏司主事陳篪〔和韶，福建莆田縣人，癸未進士〕。

同考試官
江西建昌府儒學教授劉詔〔汝承，四川江津縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
直隸真定府定州儒學學正羅釗〔彥時，福建懷安縣人，己卯貢士〕。
湖廣襄陽府襄陽縣儒學教諭胡浩〔養直，河南商城縣人，己卯貢士〕。
陝西西安府三原縣儒學教諭王冕〔宗周，山西潞州人，己卯貢士〕。
湖廣黃州府黃岡縣儒學教諭韓秉文〔敬夫，浙江慈谿縣人，壬午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Shandong Provincial Examination, Seventh Year of Jiajing (1528)

Supervising Official
Ma Jin, Investigating Censor on an inspection tour of Shandong, had the courtesy name Zongkong and was from Xuzhou, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the dingchou year.

Proctors
Guo Shao, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Kexie and was from Huozhou, Shanxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the yiwei year.
Bian Xian, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Ruming and was from Renqiu County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the xinwei year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Gu Yingxiang, Surveillance Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Weixian and was from Changxing County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.
Cheng Ying, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Xiuqing and was from Zunhua County, Shuntian Prefecture. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuchen year.

Examiners
Liu Shiyang, Supervising Secretary of the Right in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue, had the courtesy name Shifu and was from Min County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate in the dingchou year.
Chen Chi, Secretary in the Yunnan Bureau of the Ministry of Justice, had the courtesy name Heshao and was from Putian County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guiwei year.

Associate Examiners
Liu Zhao, Professor at the Confucian School of Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Rucheng and was from Jiangjin County, Sichuan. He became a tribute student (gongshi) in the guiyou year.
Luo Zhao, Instructor at the Confucian School of Dingzhou, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Yanshi and was from Huai'an County, Fujian. He became a tribute student in the jimao year.
Hu Hao, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xiangyang County, Xiangyang Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Yangzhi and was from Shangcheng County, Henan. He became a tribute student in the jimao year.
Wang Mian, Instructor at the Confucian School of Sanyuan County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, had the courtesy name Zongzhou and was from Luzhou, Shanxi. He became a tribute student in the jimao year.
Han Bingwen, Instructor at the Confucian School of Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Jingfu and was from Cixi County, Zhejiang. He became a tribute student in the renwu year.

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
正顔色斯近信矣
君子之所不可及者其唯人之所不見乎
必有事焉而勿正心勿忘勿助長也
易
善世而不伐德博而化
利見大人亨聚以正也
變則通通則久
近也柔之爲道不利遠者其要无咎其用
柔中也
===
書
帝曰來禹汝亦昌言禹拜曰都帝予何言
先王克謹天戒臣人克有常憲百官修輔
厥后惟明明每歲孟春遒人以木鐸
徇于路官師相規工執藝事以諫
惟曰欲至于萬年惟王子子孫孫永保民
下民祗若萬邦咸休
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
正顔色，斯近信矣。
君子之所不可及者，其唯人之所不見乎！
必有事焉而勿正，心勿忘，勿助長也。

易
善世而不伐，德博而化。
利見大人，亨，聚以正也。
變則通，通則久。
近也。柔之爲道，不利遠者，其要无咎，其用柔中也。

書
帝曰：「來，禹！汝亦昌言。」禹拜曰：「都！帝，予何言？」
先王克謹天戒，臣人克有常憲，百官修輔，厥后惟明。明每歲孟春，遒人以木鐸徇于路，官師相規，工執藝事以諫。
惟曰：「欲至于萬年，惟王子子孫孫永保民。」
下民祗若，萬邦咸休。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Set your countenance aright, and you will approach trustworthiness.”

“Is it not precisely in what others do not see that the gentleman cannot be equaled?”

“One must keep working at it without expecting a predetermined result; the mind must neither forget it nor help it grow.”

Book of Changes (Yijing)

“He benefits the world without boasting; his virtue is extensive and brings transformation.”

“‘It is beneficial to see the great man; success’: this is gathering together through correctness.”

“With change comes free passage; with free passage comes endurance.”

“It is near [?]. The way of yielding does not favor going far; its essential aim is freedom from blame, and its application lies in yielding while keeping to the mean.”

Book of Documents (Shangshu)

“The emperor said, ‘Come, Yu! You too should offer excellent counsel.’ Yu bowed and said, ‘Ah! O Emperor, what can I say?’”

“The former kings could heed Heaven’s warnings carefully; their subjects could maintain constant standards. The hundred officials fulfilled their duties in support, and their sovereign was enlightened. [The transcription repeats ‘enlightened’ here: 明, ?] Every year, in the first month of spring, the herald went along the roads with a wooden-tongued bell. Officials admonished one another, and artisans offered remonstrance through the work of their crafts.”

“They say only, ‘We wish this to last for ten thousand years, so that the king’s sons and grandsons, generation after generation, may forever protect the people.’”

“The common people reverently complied, and the myriad states all enjoyed well-being.”

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
詩
寬兮綽兮猗重較兮
樂只君子德音不已
樂只君子民之父母
文王在上於昭于天周雖舊邦其命維新
有周不顯帝命不時文王陟降在帝
左右
既右烈考亦右文母
春秋
夏齊侯陳侯鄭伯遇于垂〔莊公四年〕晉侯執
曹伯歸于京師〔成公十五年〕己未衛侯
出奔齊〔襄公十四年〕吳子使札來聘〔襄〕
===
公二十九年
三月宋司馬華孫來盟〔文公十五年〕夏曹公
孫會自鄸出奔宋〔昭公二十年〕
春王二月壬子宋華元帥師及鄭公子歸
生帥師戰于大棘宋師敗績獲宋華
元〔宣公二年〕公會晉師于瓦〔定公八年〕
仲孫羯會晉荀盈齊高止宋華定衛世叔
punctuated:
詩
寬兮綽兮，猗重較兮。
樂只君子，德音不已。
樂只君子，民之父母。
文王在上，於昭于天。周雖舊邦，其命維新。有周不顯，帝命不時。文王陟降，在帝左右。
既右烈考，亦右文母。

春秋
夏，齊侯、陳侯、鄭伯遇于垂。〔莊公四年〕晉侯執曹伯，歸于京師。〔成公十五年〕己未，衛侯出奔齊。〔襄公十四年〕吳子使札來聘。〔襄〕公二十九年
三月，宋司馬華孫來盟。〔文公十五年〕夏，曹公孫會自鄸出奔宋。〔昭公二十年〕
春，王二月，壬子，宋華元帥師及鄭公子歸生帥師戰于大棘，宋師敗績，獲宋華元。〔宣公二年〕公會晉師于瓦。〔定公八年〕
仲孫羯會晉荀盈、齊高止、宋華定、衛世叔
translation_en:
Book of Odes

How generous, how magnanimous! He leans against the carriage’s double crossbars.

Joyful is the noble man; his virtuous reputation never ceases.

Joyful is the noble man, the father and mother of the people.

King Wen is on high; oh, how brightly he shines in Heaven! Though Zhou was an old state, its mandate was new. Is Zhou not illustrious? Is the Lord’s mandate not timely? King Wen ascends and descends, at the Lord’s left and right.

Having aided the illustrious deceased father, he also aided the cultured mother.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In summer, the Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng met at Chui. 〔Fourth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 The Marquis of Jin seized the Earl of Cao and brought him back to the royal capital. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕 On the jiwei day, the Marquis of Wei fled to Qi. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Xiang.〕 The Viscount of Wu sent Zha on a formal visit. 〔Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang; the annotation brackets are misplaced in the transcription.〕

In the third month, Hua Sun, Minister of War of Song, came to conclude a covenant. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Wen.〕 In summer, Gongsun Hui of Cao fled from Meng to Song. 〔Twentieth year of Duke Zhao.〕

In spring, in the second month of the royal calendar, on the renzi day, Hua Yuan of Song led an army into battle at Daji against an army led by Prince Guisheng of Zheng. The army of Song suffered a crushing defeat, and Hua Yuan of Song was captured. 〔Second year of Duke Xuan.〕 The duke met the army of Jin at Wa. 〔Eighth year of Duke Ding.〕

Zhongsun Jie met with Xun Ying of Jin, Gao Zhi of Qi, Hua Ding of Song, and Shishu of Wei …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
儀鄭公孫敔曹人莒人滕人薛人小
邾人城杞〔襄公二十九年〕
禮記
聽於無聲視於無形
雖有至道弗學不知其善也是故學然後
知不足教然後知困知不足然後能
自反也知困然後能自强也
昔者舜作五絃之琴以歌南風夔始制樂
以賞諸侯
君子隱而顯不矜而莊不厲而威不言而
===
信
第貳塲
論
萬物皆備於我
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢下州郡檢覈墾田户口詔〔建武十五年〕
擬唐以戴冑爲大理少卿誥〔貞觀元年〕
擬賀
punctuated:
儀、鄭公孫敔、曹人、莒人、滕人、薛人、小邾人城杞。〔襄公二十九年〕

《禮記》
聽於無聲，視於無形。
雖有至道，弗學，不知其善也。是故學然後知不足，教然後知困。知不足，然後能自反也；知困，然後能自强也。
昔者舜作五絃之琴，以歌南風；夔始制樂，以賞諸侯。
君子隱而顯，不矜而莊，不厲而威，不言而信。

第貳塲
論
萬物皆備於我。

詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢下州郡檢覈墾田户口詔。〔建武十五年〕
擬唐以戴冑爲大理少卿誥。〔貞觀元年〕
擬賀
translation_en:
…Yi of Wei, Gongsun Yu of Zheng, and men of Cao, Ju, Teng, Xue, and Lesser Zhu fortified Qi. 〔Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang〕

Book of Rites (Liji)
Listen where there is no sound; look where there is no form.
Although there is a supreme Way, without studying it one cannot know its excellence. Thus, only after learning does one recognize one’s deficiencies; only after teaching does one recognize one’s difficulties. Recognizing one’s deficiencies, one can then examine oneself; recognizing one’s difficulties, one can then strive to improve oneself.
In ancient times, Shun made a five-stringed zither to sing “The South Wind”; Kui first instituted music to reward the regional lords.
The gentleman is unobtrusive yet manifest, dignified without self-importance, awe-inspiring without severity, and trusted without speaking.

Second Session
Discourse
All things are fully present within me.

Imperial Decrees, Investiture Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One question within this category [?]〕
Draft an imperial decree of the Han dynasty directing the provinces and commanderies to verify cultivated acreage and the numbers of households and inhabitants. 〔Fifteenth year of Jianwu〕
Draft an investiture proclamation of the Tang dynasty appointing Dai Zhou as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review. 〔First year of Zhenguan〕
Draft a congratulatory …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
萬壽聖節表
判語〔五條〕
官員赴任過限
多收稅糧斛面
僧道拜父母
蒙古色目人婚姻
不操練軍士
第叁場
策〔五道〕
===
問心學發於堯舜之授受三代之君有聖
有賢亦罔不於心學焉得之漢唐宋之
興去古漸遠心學不明其間英君誼辟
亦固有得其近似者乎洪惟我
太祖高皇帝天縱神聖能自得師心學之傳遠
接堯舜見於諭輔臣者可考也
列聖相傳益以光大我
皇上纘承丕緒正位凝命
御製敬一箴且為之序又為心箴及視聽言動
punctuated:
萬壽聖節表。

判語〔五條〕：官員赴任過限；多收稅糧斛面；僧道拜父母；蒙古色目人婚姻；不操練軍士。

第叁場
策〔五道〕

問：心學發於堯舜之授受，三代之君有聖有賢，亦罔不於心學焉得之。漢唐宋之興，去古漸遠，心學不明，其間英君誼辟，亦固有得其近似者乎？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，天縱神聖，能自得師，心學之傳遠接堯舜，見於諭輔臣者可考也。列聖相傳，益以光大。我皇上纘承丕緒，正位凝命，御製《敬一箴》，且為之序，又為《心箴》及視聽言動
translation_en:
…a memorial for the Sacred Festival of Imperial Longevity [the emperor’s birthday].

Legal judgments [five items]: Officials exceeding the time limit for taking up their posts; collecting excess tax grain above the level of the measuring vessel; Buddhist monks and Daoist priests bowing to their parents; marriages of Mongols and Semu people; failure to drill soldiers.

Third Session
Policy questions [five questions]

Question: The learning of the mind originated in the transmission from Yao to Shun. Among the rulers of the Three Dynasties were sages and worthies, and all derived their attainments from the learning of the mind. With the rise of the Han, Tang, and Song, antiquity grew increasingly distant, and the learning of the mind became obscure. Were there nevertheless outstanding and righteous sovereigns among them who attained something approximating it?

We reverently consider that our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom, was able to find a teacher for himself. His transmission of the learning of the mind reached back across the ages to Yao and Shun; this can be examined in his instructions to his assisting ministers. Successive sage emperors transmitted it and further extended its brilliance. Our present emperor has inherited this great legacy, assumed his rightful position, and secured Heaven’s mandate. He personally composed the Admonition on Reverence and Oneness (Jingyi zhen), together with a preface, and also wrote on the Admonition on the Mind and on seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
四箴解
聖謨洋洋發明心學究極本原斯固
皇上生知之聖獨得之天也不知
聖功何所脩為抑將何所徵驗歟所謂敬一即
精一歟與
聖祖之言亦有合歟今
聖上春秋方盛日新月益尚有進於是者乎是
未可但已也茲欲輔成
君德襄翊太平果有何要言急務可以獻于
===
廷乎願陳之以為
天地博厚高明悠久之助
問六經者先王經世之要道夫子删述以
垂憲萬世者也顏曾思孟相繼傳述孟
子沒而其傳泯矣遭秦焚書經學益晦
漢興稍稍振起而齊魯之間專門名家
者何限豈不以師友淵源所在自有不
得而泯滅者與今姑舉一二與諸士論
之在魯則有申公之詩高堂生之禮江
punctuated:
四箴解。聖謨洋洋，發明心學，究極本原。斯固皇上生知之聖，獨得之天也。不知聖功何所脩為，抑將何所徵驗歟？所謂敬一，即精一歟？與聖祖之言亦有合歟？今聖上春秋方盛，日新月益，尚有進於是者乎？是未可但已也。茲欲輔成君德，襄翊太平，果有何要言急務可以獻于廷乎？願陳之，以為天地博厚高明悠久之助。

問：六經者，先王經世之要道，夫子删述以垂憲萬世者也。顏、曾、思、孟相繼傳述，孟子沒而其傳泯矣。遭秦焚書，經學益晦。漢興，稍稍振起，而齊魯之間專門名家者何限！豈不以師友淵源所在，自有不得而泯滅者與？今姑舉一二，與諸士論之。在魯，則有申公之詩、高堂生之禮、江
translation_en:
…explanations of the Four Admonitions. The imperial teachings are vast and abundant: they elucidate the learning of the mind and probe its ultimate source. This surely reflects His Majesty’s innate sagely knowledge, received uniquely from Heaven. Yet through what cultivation is his sagely achievement developed, and by what may it be verified? Is what is called “reverent single-mindedness” the same as “refinement and single-mindedness”? Does it also accord with the words of the sagely founder? His Majesty is now in the prime of life, renewing himself daily and advancing monthly. Is there further progress to be made beyond this? Surely one cannot simply stop here. If we now wish to help perfect the ruler’s virtue and assist in bringing about universal peace, what essential counsels and urgent measures can we present at court? Please set them forth, to help him attain the breadth and depth, loftiness and brilliance, and enduring constancy of Heaven and Earth.

Question: The Six Classics contain the essential Way by which the former kings ordered the world. The Master edited and transmitted them to provide models for all ages. Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, Zisi, and Mengzi transmitted and expounded them in succession; after Mengzi died, however, this transmission faded away. With the burning of books under the Qin, classical learning became still more obscure. After the Han arose, it gradually revived, and among the scholars of Qi and Lu, how countless were those renowned for specializing in particular traditions! Was this not because the traditions flowing through teachers and friends contained something that could never be extinguished? Let us now take one or two examples for discussion with you scholars. In Lu there were Shen Gong’s teaching of the Book of Odes, Gaotang Sheng’s teaching of the Rites, and Jiang…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
公之春秋夏侯之尚書孟喜之易而王
式匡衡之徒又皆以詩名者也在齊則
有伏生之書轅固之詩胡毋生之春秋
梁丘賀之易而兒寬歐陽歙之徒又皆
以書名者也其源流授受之迹亦有可
言者與其所傳述亦有得於六經之旨
否與夫諸儒有出爲世用者矣迹其行
事亦皆有可觀與夫當秦火旣熾經學
不明微諸賢相繼而表章之道幾乎息
===
矣而皆不與其得斯道之傳者何與或
者有謂秦焚書而書存諸儒窮經而經
絕然則諸儒之窮經者適足以害道與
毋乃言之過矣子諸生生於齊魯之邦
其優劣得失講之熟矣抑將何所取法
與願備言之以觀尚友之學
問儀禮全經散逸今傳者僅十七篇然品
式度數從可稽已姑舉數篇與諸子論
之覲禮著侯氏勞賜朝享之節明矣然
punctuated:
公之春秋、夏侯之尚書、孟喜之易，而王式、匡衡之徒又皆以詩名者也。在齊則有伏生之書、轅固之詩、胡毋生之春秋、梁丘賀之易，而兒寬、歐陽歙之徒又皆以書名者也。其源流授受之迹，亦有可言者與？其所傳述，亦有得於六經之旨否與？夫諸儒有出爲世用者矣，迹其行事，亦皆有可觀與？夫當秦火旣熾，經學不明，微諸賢相繼而表章之，道幾乎息矣，而皆不與其得斯道之傳者，何與？或者有謂秦焚書而書存，諸儒窮經而經絕，然則諸儒之窮經者，適足以害道與？毋乃言之過矣！子諸生生於齊魯之邦，其優劣得失講之熟矣，抑將何所取法與？願備言之，以觀尚友之學。
問：儀禮全經散逸，今傳者僅十七篇，然品式度數從可稽已。姑舉數篇與諸子論之。覲禮著侯氏勞賜朝享之節明矣，然
translation_en:
…Gong’s teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals, Xiahou’s of the Book of Documents, and Meng Xi’s of the Book of Changes; Wang Shi, Kuang Heng, and others were also all renowned for the Book of Odes. In Qi there were Fu Sheng’s teaching of the Book of Documents, Yuan Gu’s of the Book of Odes, Humu Sheng’s of the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Liangqiu He’s of the Book of Changes; Ni Kuan, Ouyang Xi, and others were also all renowned for the Book of Documents. Can you give an account of the origins and development of these traditions and the traces of their transmission from teacher to pupil? Did what they transmitted and expounded grasp the purport of the Six Classics? Some of these scholars entered public service: if we examine their conduct, was it in every case worthy of regard? When the fires of Qin’s book burning had blazed and classical learning had become obscure, had these worthies not successively elucidated and honored it, the Way would almost have died out. Why, then, are none of them counted among those who received the transmission of this Way? Some say, “Qin burned the books, yet the books survived; the scholars exhaustively studied the Classics, yet the Classics’ transmission was severed.” Does this mean that these scholars’ exhaustive study of the Classics served only to harm the Way? Surely this is an overstatement! You students were born in the lands of Qi and Lu and have thoroughly discussed these scholars’ strengths and weaknesses, achievements and failings. Whom, then, will you take as your models? Please explain fully, so that we may assess your learning in taking the ancients as friends.
Question: The complete text of the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) has been dispersed and lost; only seventeen chapters are now transmitted. Nevertheless, its prescribed forms, measures, and numbers can still be ascertained [?]. Let us select a few chapters to discuss with you. The chapter “Audience with the Son of Heaven” clearly sets out the procedures for welcoming and bestowing gifts upon the feudal lords, their audience at court, and their presentation of offerings. Yet…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
公侯伯子男圭冕車牢朝位擯介以至
於饗食問勞之數斯經不載其詳乃見
於周禮何歟少牢饋食著位序鼎俎尊
罍豆籩迎尸羞獻蕃㲼之禮詳矣則又
有儐尸於堂之禮豈以獻酬之禮未備
陽厭之祭未舉歟昏禮有對筵合巹見
婦于舅姑贄醴婦婦盥饋舅姑饗婦之
節則有昏義可考矣說者復有疑於饗
婦奠酬之未詳亦可推其義歟然必三
月而後廟見者何也今之人有行者固
===
一一如斯禮乎鄉飲酒禮有祭薦祭酒
嚌肺啐酒有不拜洗不嚌肺不啐酒不
告旨之節亦有鄉飲酒義可考矣鄭玄
註賓主介遵衆賓之位亦與記禮者之
說合歟其所謂賓主介遵以及衆賓者
孰為之也今有司所行者即斯禮無異
乎夫覲以嚴君臣祭以明父子昏以重
夫婦鄉飲酒以序長幼禮之大體于是
punctuated: 公侯伯子男圭冕車牢、朝位擯介，以至於饗食問勞之數，斯經不載其詳，乃見於《周禮》，何歟？《少牢饋食》著位序、鼎俎、尊罍、豆籩、迎尸、羞獻、蕃㲼之禮詳矣，則又有儐尸於堂之禮，豈以獻酬之禮未備，陽厭之祭未舉歟？昏禮有對筵合巹、見婦于舅姑、贄、醴婦、婦盥饋、舅姑饗婦之節，則有《昏義》可考矣。說者復有疑於饗婦奠酬之未詳，亦可推其義歟？然必三月而後廟見者，何也？今之人有行者，固一一如斯禮乎？鄉飲酒禮有祭薦、祭酒、嚌肺、啐酒，有不拜洗、不嚌肺、不啐酒、不告旨之節，亦有《鄉飲酒義》可考矣。鄭玄註賓主介遵衆賓之位，亦與記禮者之說合歟？其所謂賓主介遵以及衆賓者，孰為之也？今有司所行者，即斯禮無異乎？夫覲以嚴君臣，祭以明父子，昏以重夫婦，鄉飲酒以序長幼，禮之大體于是
translation_en:
…As for the jade tablets, ceremonial caps, carriages, sacrificial animals, court positions, ushers, and attendants appropriate to dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons, and even the prescribed particulars of banquets, meals, inquiries, and greetings, this classic does not record them in detail; instead, they appear in the Rites of Zhou. Why is this? The chapter “Food Offerings with the Lesser Set of Sacrificial Animals” gives detailed accounts of the rites governing positions and precedence, cauldrons and offering stands, wine vessels and jars, wooden dishes and bamboo baskets, welcoming the impersonator of the deceased, presenting offerings, and “fan yi” [?]. Yet there is also a rite for entertaining the impersonator as a guest in the hall. Is this because the rites of presenting and reciprocating wine have not yet been completed, and the yangyan sacrifice—the presentation of offerings without an impersonator in the illuminated part of the room—has not yet been performed?

The marriage rites include facing one another on mats and drinking from the paired halves of a gourd, presenting the bride to her parents-in-law, presenting gifts, offering sweet wine to the bride, the bride washing her hands and serving food, and the parents-in-law entertaining the bride. The chapter “The Meaning of the Marriage Rites” may be consulted concerning these. Commentators nevertheless express doubts about the lack of detail concerning setting down the cup of reciprocal wine when entertaining the bride. Can the meaning of this, too, be inferred? Why, however, must three months pass before the bride is presented in the ancestral temple? Do those who perform these ceremonies today really follow these rites in every particular?

The district drinking ceremony includes offering portions of the foods set out, offering a libation, tasting the lung, and sipping the wine. It also includes occasions on which one does not bow at the washing of the cup, taste the lung, sip the wine, or announce its fine flavor. The chapter “The Meaning of the District Drinking Ceremony” may likewise be consulted. Does Zheng Xuan’s commentary on the positions of the principal guest, host, assistant guest, honored guests, and other guests also agree with the account of those who recorded the rites? Who serves in these capacities as principal guest, host, assistant guest, honored guests, and other guests? Is the ceremony now performed by the responsible officials identical to this rite, without any differences?

Court audiences give solemn expression to the relationship between ruler and minister; sacrifices make clear that between father and son; marriage gives weight to that between husband and wife; and district drinking establishes precedence between elders and juniors. The essential principles of ritual herein…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
手在了此則諸篇可以類推而古禮可
以行於今措之國家有餘用矣請詳對
以觀禮學
問刑以弼教古聖帝明王不能舍是而為
治也稽諸典謨周禮可見已彼呂刑一
篇哀矜惻怛猶可以想見三代忠厚之
遺意說者猶病其濫贖以謂穆王為此
一切權宜之術以歛民財耳其信然歟
後世願治之君遂至除肉刑不用然則
古帝王之制非歟又有著政論病夫刑
===
之寬者然則刑固貴嚴歟我
聖祖折衷前代制為
大明律遵行至今
皇上以好生為德慎重民命屢
詔䘏刑中外百司奉行惟謹夫有一定之律值
此維新之治而未見夫刑清訟簡者何
也豈所謂有德惟刑哀敬折獄者固難
事歟抑今民非古醇厚之民歟晦菴朱
punctuated:
手在。了此，則諸篇可以類推，而古禮可以行於今，措之國家有餘用矣。請詳對，以觀禮學。

問：刑以弼教，古聖帝明王不能舍是而為治也。稽諸典謨、周禮，可見已。彼呂刑一篇，哀矜惻怛，猶可以想見三代忠厚之遺意。說者猶病其濫贖，以謂穆王為此一切權宜之術，以歛民財耳。其信然歟？後世願治之君，遂至除肉刑不用，然則古帝王之制非歟？又有著政論，病夫刑之寬者，然則刑固貴嚴歟？我聖祖折衷前代，制為《大明律》，遵行至今。皇上以好生為德，慎重民命，屢詔䘏刑，中外百司奉行惟謹。夫有一定之律，值此維新之治，而未見夫刑清訟簡者，何也？豈所謂有德惟刑、哀敬折獄者，固難事歟？抑今民非古醇厚之民歟？晦菴朱
translation_en:
… lies here [?]. Once this is understood, the other chapters can be inferred by analogy, and ancient rites can be practiced today; applied to the affairs of the state, they will be more than sufficient. Please answer in detail, so that we may assess your learning in ritual.

Question: Punishments serve to support moral instruction. The sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity could not dispense with them in governing. This can be seen by examining the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents and the Rites of Zhou. In the chapter “The Punishments of Lü,” its compassion and heartfelt solicitude still allow us to imagine the enduring spirit of loyalty and generosity of the Three Dynasties. Yet commentators criticize its excessive use of redemption payments, saying that King Mu devised this expedient merely to extract wealth from the people. Is this really so? In later ages, rulers who sought good government went so far as to abolish mutilating punishments. Does this mean that the institutions of the ancient emperors and kings were wrong? Others, writing discourses on government, criticized the leniency of punishments. Does this mean that severity is indeed what matters in punishment? Our sagely founding ancestor weighed the precedents of earlier dynasties and established the Great Ming Code, which has been observed down to the present. His Majesty takes cherishing life as a virtue and treats the lives of the people with great care. He has repeatedly issued edicts enjoining compassion in administering punishment, and officials in every office, at court and throughout the provinces, have implemented them with utmost diligence. Given an established code and this era of renewed governance, why have we still not seen equitable administration of punishments and fewer lawsuits? Is what is meant by ‘only the virtuous should administer punishments’ and ‘deciding cases with compassion and reverence’ inherently difficult to accomplish? Or are the people of today no longer as honest and generous as those of antiquity? Zhu, known as Hui’an …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
子嘗有論著眞卹刑之至要也可得聞
其詳歟茲欲使民得其分百司得其職
刑書胥占不失
聖朝制作之意辟以止辟仰贊
聖上好生之德其道安在諸士子出而服官斯
亦致用之一也幸明言以教我
問國有荒政所以恤民今水旱相仍螟蝗
遍野害至百千里稼穡空矣何以為賑
卹之方夫欲歸之天數則脩德所宜先
欲圖之人事則舉政不可後顧安使災
害不生乎國有力役所以興事今漕河
淤淺疏鑿他道役至數萬人民力竭矣
何以為休息之議夫欲底績新河則勞
費惟艱欲疏通舊道則壅塞漫衍豈終
無經久之猷乎賦歛以足軍國之需
國家取民旣有定則矣財貨所聚非官則民
今蠲免之
詔屢下而民不益富何邪或謂貪吏姦民之囊
punctuated:
子嘗有論著，眞卹刑之至要也，可得聞其詳歟？茲欲使民得其分，百司得其職，刑書胥占，不失聖朝制作之意，辟以止辟，仰贊聖上好生之德，其道安在？諸士子出而服官，斯亦致用之一也，幸明言以教我。

問：國有荒政，所以恤民。今水旱相仍，螟蝗遍野，害至百千里，稼穡空矣，何以為賑卹之方？夫欲歸之天數，則脩德所宜先；欲圖之人事，則舉政不可後。顧安使災害不生乎？國有力役，所以興事。今漕河淤淺，疏鑿他道，役至數萬人，民力竭矣，何以為休息之議？夫欲底績新河，則勞費惟艱；欲疏通舊道，則壅塞漫衍。豈終無經久之猷乎？賦歛以足軍國之需，國家取民旣有定則矣。財貨所聚，非官則民。今蠲免之詔屢下，而民不益富，何邪？或謂貪吏姦民之囊
translation_en:
…Master Zhu once wrote on this subject, setting out the very essentials of compassion in administering punishment. May we hear these explained in detail? We now wish to ensure that the people receive their due and that all officials fulfill their duties; that penal writings and clerical consultation [?] do not depart from the intent behind the august dynasty’s institutions; and that punishments serve to end punishment, thereby supporting His Majesty’s virtue of cherishing life. By what means can this be achieved? When you candidates enter official service, this too will be one way to put your learning into practice. Please explain clearly and instruct me.

Question: The state has measures for famine relief by which to care for the people. Now floods and droughts follow one another, and grain pests and locusts fill the fields. The damage extends for hundreds and thousands of li, and the crops are gone. What methods should be adopted for relief? If we would attribute this to Heaven’s allotted course, cultivating virtue should come first; if we would address it through human affairs, implementing measures of government must not be delayed. How, then, can we prevent disasters from arising? The state imposes labor service to undertake public works. Now the grain-transport canal is silted up and shallow, and alternative channels are being dredged and excavated. Tens of thousands of men have been conscripted, and the people’s strength is exhausted. What proposals can give them respite? If we would complete the new canal, the labor and expense present great difficulties; if we would clear the old course, there are obstructions and spreading overflow. Can there ultimately be no enduring plan? Taxes and levies supply the needs of the military and the state, and the state already has fixed rules governing what it takes from the people. Wealth accumulates either with the government or with the people. Now edicts granting tax remissions have repeatedly been issued, yet the people grow no richer. Why is this? Some say that the purses of corrupt officials and unscrupulous commoners…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
稟或謂民俗奢侈之害財其何以富民
而足國用乎盜賊迫於饑寒之計
朝廷惻惻時見撫綏矣好生惡死人心所同
今勦捕之兵時出而民不自愛何邪或
咎有司撫馭之無方或咎承平武備之
不競其何以安民而儆無虞乎是四者
乃生民休戚天下治忽所係諸生觸目
激衷必有大緼藉欲言者幸著于篇以
觀濟時之學
punctuated: 稟，或謂民俗奢侈之害財。其何以富民而足國用乎？盜賊迫於饑寒之計，朝廷惻惻，時見撫綏矣。好生惡死，人心所同，今勦捕之兵時出，而民不自愛，何邪？或咎有司撫馭之無方，或咎承平武備之不競。其何以安民而儆無虞乎？是四者，乃生民休戚、天下治忽所係。諸生觸目激衷，必有大緼藉欲言者，幸著于篇，以觀濟時之學。
translation_en: …stores [?]; others say that extravagant popular habits deplete wealth. How, then, can the people be enriched while sufficient resources are provided for the state's needs? Bandits are driven to their livelihood by hunger and cold. The court, deeply compassionate, has repeatedly shown its concern by pacifying and reassuring them. Love of life and aversion to death are common to all human hearts. Yet although troops are repeatedly dispatched to suppress and apprehend bandits, the people do not cherish their own lives. Why is this? Some blame the responsible officials for lacking effective methods of conciliation and control; others blame the weakness of military preparedness during prolonged peace. How, then, can the people be brought security while vigilance is maintained in times free of trouble? These four matters bear upon the people's well-being and suffering, and upon order and disorder throughout the realm. You candidates, stirred in your hearts by what you see, must have substantial stores of learning that you wish to express. Please set them forth in your essays, so that we may assess your learning for addressing the needs of the times.

同考試官學正羅　批〔此題繫於政體樹德〕
〔儀民之道備焉塲中率多剽拾陳語可厭録〕
〔是作者壯其理致精邃辭氣莊嚴正色讀之〕
〔亦可想見其風釆矣〕
考試官主事陳　批〔筆力老健佳士也〕
考試官右給事中劉　批〔文亦近信宜録〕
===
端於面而協乎誠此君子之所重也盖顔色之
正難乎其信也正而信焉豈非道之所在君子
之所重者哉昔曾子告孟敬子至是盖謂君子
重道於三事而實不外乎一身固有所謂動容
貌遠暴慢矣彼見於面者有顔色焉毋傾毋田
舉合乎當然之則而康而色不踰乎至正之規
時乎動止隨地而著見凝重於手釆者自足以
起人之景仰有所謂君子之光者矣時乎應酬
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
正顔色，斯近信矣。
王得民

同考試官學正羅批〔此題繫於政體，樹德〕〔儀民之道備焉。塲中率多剽拾陳語，可厭。録〕〔是作者，壯其理致精邃，辭氣莊嚴。正色讀之，〕〔亦可想見其風釆矣。〕
考試官主事陳批〔筆力老健，佳士也。〕
考試官右給事中劉批〔文亦近信，宜録。〕

端於面而協乎誠，此君子之所重也。盖顔色之正，難乎其信也。正而信焉，豈非道之所在、君子之所重者哉？昔曾子告孟敬子，至是盖謂君子重道於三事，而實不外乎一身。固有所謂動容貌遠暴慢矣。彼見於面者，有顔色焉。毋傾毋田，舉合乎當然之則；而康而色，不踰乎至正之規。時乎動止，隨地而著見，凝重於手釆者，自足以起人之景仰，有所謂君子之光者矣。時乎應酬，
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“When one makes one’s countenance correct, one approaches trustworthiness.”
Wang Demin

Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, School Instructor: “This topic concerns the substance of government and encompasses the way of establishing virtue and serving as a model for the people. Most answers in this examination merely pilfer stale expressions—wearisome indeed. We have selected this author’s work in admiration of its profound and refined reasoning and its dignified language and tone. Reading it with a solemn countenance, one can also imagine the author’s bearing.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Bureau Secretary: “His writing is mature and vigorous. A fine scholar.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Supervising Secretary of the Right: “The composition, too, approaches trustworthiness. It merits selection.”

To be upright in countenance and accord with sincerity: this is what the gentleman values. For in making one’s countenance correct, the difficulty lies in making it trustworthy. If it is both correct and trustworthy, is this not where the Way resides, and what the gentleman values? When Zengzi spoke to Meng Jingzi, at this point he meant that the gentleman prizes the Way in three matters, yet these in fact extend no further than his own person. There is indeed the saying that, in moving and composing his appearance, he keeps violence and arrogance at a distance. What appears upon the face is its expression. Let it be neither tilted nor “tian” [?], so that every movement accords with the proper standard; “composed in your expression” [?], let it not exceed the bounds of perfect rectitude. In movement and repose, this manifests itself wherever he is. The gravity of his bearing [?] is itself sufficient to inspire others’ admiration: this is what is called the gentleman’s radiance. When responding to others in social exchanges, …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
隨事而呈露端莊於顏面者自足以肅人之觀
瞻有所謂維民之則者矣然其迹若涉於作為
而皆本乎實緼藉攸形罔致飾以徇外功若孅
於脩飭而皆近乎誠篤厚不掩無僞為以欺人
之衆之凝重乃其中心之敷溢有乎顯若非不
情也道不於是而在乎顏面之端莊乃其顛實
之揚休英華發外非虚妄也道不即此而存乎
夫正顏色而近信道之切於身者如此固君子
之所重而為政者之所當知也與嗟夫容貌顏
===
色辭氣三事皆脩身之要為政之本君子所貴
乎道者固惟在此彼器數之末不與焉曲禮之
毋不敬儼若思安定辭即此三事而終以安民
則聖賢相傳脩身為政之常法從可知矣曾子
守約深造此其所自得者故舉為孟敬子告彼
敬子者亦紹聞而衣德言哉
君子之所不可及者其唯人之所不見乎
王恩
同考試官教諭韓　批〔題本平易作者多涉〕
punctuated:
隨事而呈露，端莊於顏面者，自足以肅人之觀瞻，有所謂維民之則者矣。然其迹若涉於作為，而皆本乎實，緼藉攸形，罔致飾以徇外；功若孅於脩飭，而皆近乎誠，篤厚不掩，無僞為以欺人。之衆之凝重，乃其中心之敷溢，有乎顯若，非不情也，道不於是而在乎？顏面之端莊，乃其顛實之揚休，英華發外，非虚妄也，道不即此而存乎？夫正顏色而近信，道之切於身者如此，固君子之所重，而為政者之所當知也與！嗟夫！容貌、顏色、辭氣，三事皆脩身之要、為政之本。君子所貴乎道者，固惟在此，彼器數之末不與焉。《曲禮》之「毋不敬，儼若思，安定辭」，即此三事，而終以安民，則聖賢相傳脩身為政之常法，從可知矣。曾子守約深造，此其所自得者，故舉為孟敬子告。彼敬子者，亦紹聞而衣德言哉！
君子之所不可及者，其唯人之所不見乎？
王恩
同考試官教諭韓，批〔題本平易，作者多涉〕
translation_en:
…as it manifests itself in response to each affair, the dignity displayed in the face suffices to inspire reverence in those who behold it. This is what is meant by being “a model for the people.” Yet although its outward traces may seem contrived, they are all rooted in substance: inward cultivation finds expression without embellishment intended merely for outward display. Although the effort may seem excessively fine in its cultivation of deportment, it all approaches sincerity: earnestness and generosity remain unconcealed, with no artificial conduct to deceive others. This gravity [?] is the overflowing of what is within the heart, visibly manifest and not insincere. Is this not where the Way resides? The dignity of the face is the glorious expression of its inner substance [?]; its finest qualities radiate outward and are neither empty nor false. Does the Way not subsist precisely here?
To compose one’s countenance and thereby approach trustworthiness: such is the Way’s immediate bearing upon one’s own person. Surely this is what the gentleman values and what those who govern ought to understand! Ah! Deportment, countenance, and the tone of one’s speech: all three are essentials of self-cultivation and foundations of government. What the gentleman prizes in the Way lies precisely here; the minor details of ritual vessels and their prescribed numbers have no part in it. The injunctions in “Summary of the Rules of Propriety” (Quli)—“Be reverent in all things; maintain a solemn bearing as though reflecting; speak calmly and deliberately”—are these very three matters, and the passage concludes with bringing peace to the people. From this we may understand the enduring method of self-cultivation and government transmitted by sages and worthies. Zengzi held fast to the essentials and attained profound understanding. These were insights he had gained for himself, and thus he set them forth in advising Meng Jingzi. Would Jingzi, in turn, receive this teaching and clothe himself in these words of virtue?
“Is it perhaps in what others do not see that the gentleman cannot be equaled?”
Wang En.
Comment by Associate Examiner Han, Instructor: 〔The topic is fundamentally straightforward, but writers often stray into…〕

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
于牽强此篇詞不費而理足蓋嘗究心于理
學者也宜録出以為後學式
同考試官教諭胡　批　不可及正在所不見
處作者每於上句先濫說至下句又欠發明
辭嚴義精無踰于此宜録之
考試官主事陳　批　詞簡意足說理之文也
考試官右給事中劉　批　作者似此體認絕少
中庸論君子之過乎人者在能謹其獨也蓋獨
者人所不見而易忽焉者也惟君子能謹之其
===
所不可及者豈外於是哉中庸卒章引小雅正
月之詩申言君子謹獨之事若曰欲知入德之
事盍自君子過人者求之乎夫君子望重于時
人皆視之以為準名稱其實衆皆慕之以為高
匪自亢而獨立也固自有難與之並迥然出類
跂予而不可到焉者也非立異以絕俗也固自
有莫與之齊超然桉萃仰止而不可攀焉者也
是果安在也哉唯曰理欲之分動於隱微人之
所不見也於焉謹其分於念慮方萌之始而檢
punctuated:
于牽强。此篇詞不費而理足，蓋嘗究心于理學者也，宜録出以為後學式。
同考試官教諭胡批：不可及正在所不見處，作者每於上句先濫說，至下句又欠發明。辭嚴義精，無踰于此，宜録之。
考試官主事陳批：詞簡意足，說理之文也。
考試官右給事中劉批：作者似此體認絕少。
《中庸》論君子之過乎人者，在能謹其獨也。蓋獨者，人所不見而易忽焉者也，惟君子能謹之。其所不可及者，豈外於是哉？《中庸》卒章引《小雅·正月》之詩，申言君子謹獨之事，若曰：欲知入德之事，盍自君子過人者求之乎？夫君子望重于時，人皆視之以為準；名稱其實，衆皆慕之以為高。匪自亢而獨立也，固自有難與之並，迥然出類，跂予而不可到焉者也；非立異以絕俗也，固自有莫與之齊，超然桉萃，仰止而不可攀焉者也。是果安在也哉？唯曰：理欲之分，動於隱微，人之所不見也。於焉謹其分，於念慮方萌之始而檢
translation_en:
…into forced interpretations. This essay uses no unnecessary words yet fully conveys the principle. Its author has evidently devoted careful thought to the learning of principle. It should be selected as a model for later students.
Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: The very point at which others cannot match the gentleman lies in what people do not see. Writers commonly begin with indiscriminate discussion of the first clause and then fail adequately to elucidate the second. In precision of expression and refinement of meaning, nothing surpasses this essay. It should be selected.
Examiner Chen, Bureau Secretary, comments: Concise in wording and complete in meaning: an essay that elucidates principle.
Examiner Liu, Supervising Secretary of the Right, comments: Authors with such an inward understanding are exceedingly rare.
The Doctrine of the Mean explains that the gentleman surpasses others through his capacity for watchfulness over himself when alone. For solitude concerns what others do not see and what one easily neglects. Only the gentleman can maintain watchfulness over it. Could the respect in which others cannot match him lie anywhere outside this? The final chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean quotes the poem “First Month” from the Lesser Odes, further explaining the gentleman’s watchfulness when alone. It is as though it says: If you wish to understand how to enter into virtue, why not seek it in that by which the gentleman surpasses others?
The gentleman commands great esteem in his age, and everyone looks to him as a standard. His reputation accords with his actual qualities, and all admire him as exalted. He does not raise himself up in order to stand apart; rather, there is inherently something in him that others can hardly equal, setting him far above his kind, beyond reach even when they stand on tiptoe [?]. He does not cultivate eccentricity to sever himself from common society; rather, there is inherently something in him that none can match, raising him above the multitude [?], so that people look up to him but cannot climb to his height.
Where, then, does this truly reside? It is simply this: the distinction between principle and desire stirs in the hidden and subtle realm that others do not see. Here he attends carefully to that distinction, at the very inception of thoughts and deliberations, and keeps them in check…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
防之必周天人之幾介於潛伏吾之所獨知也
於焉審其幾於吾心獨覺之時而察治之益密
兢業不懈於反觀使發於心者無愧於心蓋自
脩之深功也而夫人每懈焉此其所以不可及
乎寔畏不忽於內省俾起於志者無惡於志蓋
克己之實學也而衆人恒忽焉斯其所以過於
人乎是則君子爲己謹獨之事知此學者宜亦
知所入德矣抑謹獨乃聖賢相傳爲學之要易
所謂介書所謂微皆是道也故中庸首章先乎
===
戒懼而此則先乎謹獨蓋光致意焉者也是故
德始於一幾而功臻乎位育皆自夫一心爲之
也學者誠知子思子立言之意則下學上達由
明而誠固不容用意高遠而其幾在我矣是亦
中庸之道歟
必有事焉而勿正心勿忘勿助長也
唐文
同考試官教授劉　批　〔塲中作者類以勿忘〕
意思条講在有事上至於勿正語句又與勿
punctuated:
防之必周。天人之幾，介於潛伏，吾之所獨知也；於焉審其幾於吾心獨覺之時，而察治之益密。兢業不懈於反觀，使發於心者無愧於心，蓋自脩之深功也，而夫人每懈焉，此其所以不可及乎？寔畏不忽於內省，俾起於志者無惡於志，蓋克己之實學也，而衆人恒忽焉，斯其所以過於人乎？是則君子爲己謹獨之事，知此，學者宜亦知所入德矣。抑謹獨乃聖賢相傳爲學之要，《易》所謂介，《書》所謂微，皆是道也。故《中庸》首章先乎戒懼，而此則先乎謹獨，蓋光致意焉者也。是故德始於一幾，而功臻乎位育，皆自夫一心爲之也。學者誠知子思子立言之意，則下學上達，由明而誠，固不容用意高遠，而其幾在我矣。是亦《中庸》之道歟？
必有事焉而勿正，心勿忘，勿助長也。
唐文。
同考試官教授劉，批：〔塲中作者類以勿忘〕意思条講在有事上，至於勿正語句，又與勿
translation_en:
…and make the safeguards thorough. The subtle juncture between Heaven and human desire lies concealed, known to oneself alone. There one examines it at the moment when one’s own mind alone becomes aware of it, making scrutiny and correction still more exact. Remaining vigilant and diligent, never slackening in inward reflection, one ensures that whatever issues from the mind gives the mind no cause for shame. This is the profound work of self-cultivation, yet people commonly neglect it. Is this why they cannot equal the gentleman? Maintaining genuine reverence and apprehension, never neglecting inward examination, one ensures that whatever arises in the will leaves the will without evil. This is the practical learning of overcoming oneself, yet ordinary people constantly disregard it. Is this why he surpasses others? Such is the gentleman’s work of learning for his own sake and exercising vigilance when alone. Knowing this, students should also know how to enter into virtue.
Moreover, vigilance when alone is the essential principle of learning transmitted from sage to worthy. What the Book of Changes calls the subtle juncture, and what the Book of Documents calls the minute, both refer to this Way. Thus the opening chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean gives precedence to caution and apprehension, whereas here precedence is given to vigilance when alone: this is where particular emphasis is placed [?]. Virtue therefore begins in a single incipient stirring, while its achievement extends to Heaven and Earth taking their proper places and the myriad things being nurtured. All this is accomplished through the one mind. If students truly understand Master Zisi’s intention in setting forth his teaching, then, learning below and reaching understanding above, proceeding from understanding to sincerity, they surely must not direct their aspirations toward what is lofty and remote: the decisive beginning lies within themselves. Is this not also the Way of the Doctrine of the Mean?
“One must have something to work at, yet must not anticipate results; the mind must not forget it, nor must one help it grow.”
Tang Wen.
Associate Examiner Liu, an Education Professor, comments: 〔Writers in the examination hall generally take “must not forget”〕 and expound its meaning clause by clause [?] under “have something to work at.” As for the phrase “must not anticipate results,” they again fail to distinguish it from “must not …”

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
助無所分别殊為可厭此篇體認親切亦可
以覘子之知養氣矣錄之以式
考試官主事陳　批　文整而氣足可式
考試官右給事中劉　批　說理精切
大賢之論養氣在得其養而無所害焉夫氣之
生於集義也尚矣有事勿忘而戒於正助斯其
為善養者乎昔孟子答公孫丑之問及此若曰
浩然之氣生於義之集而餒於義之襲義不容
外矣故必致力於吾身凡有云為由中制外惟
===
集義之是務庸功於攸行凡厭酬酢以心度宜
惟集義之是圖有事可矣若乃力始至而遂期
其效見小欲速之不免功纔施而預計其成先
難後獲之罔知是力道之念奪於徇外自得之
學論於近功矣奚可哉夫氣充於義之集而或
有所未充功不容已也但當益力於有事而持
之以悠久不容須臾之或息常反於集義而持
之以歲月毋使頃刻之或忘勿忘可矣若乃飾
虛為盈不由中出而作為以助其長矯弱為强
punctuated:
助無所分别，殊為可厭。此篇體認親切，亦可以覘子之知養氣矣。錄之以式。
考試官主事陳，批：文整而氣足，可式。
考試官右給事中劉，批：說理精切。
大賢之論養氣，在得其養而無所害焉。夫氣之生於集義也尚矣，有事勿忘而戒於正助，斯其為善養者乎？昔孟子答公孫丑之問及此，若曰：浩然之氣生於義之集，而餒於義之襲，義不容外矣。故必致力於吾身，凡有云為，由中制外，惟集義之是務；庸功於攸行，凡厭酬酢，以心度宜，惟集義之是圖。有事可矣。若乃力始至而遂期其效，見小欲速之不免；功纔施而預計其成，先難後獲之罔知，是力道之念奪於徇外，自得之學論於近功矣，奚可哉？夫氣充於義之集，而或有所未充，功不容已也。但當益力於有事，而持之以悠久，不容須臾之或息；常反於集義，而持之以歲月，毋使頃刻之或忘。勿忘可矣。若乃飾虛為盈，不由中出而作為以助其長；矯弱為强，
translation_en:
…“assisting its growth” is not distinguished at all—a most objectionable fault. This essay shows an intimate and exact understanding; it also allows one to discern your knowledge of how to nourish vital energy. It is recorded here as a model.
Examiner Chen, a Bureau Secretary, comments: “The composition is orderly and its energy ample. It can serve as a model.”
Examiner Liu, a Supervising Secretary of the Right, comments: “The exposition of principle is precise and penetrating.”
The great worthy’s discussion of nourishing vital energy concerns giving it proper nourishment without causing it harm. That vital energy arises from the accumulation of righteousness is a long-established teaching. To keep working at it and not forget, while guarding against anticipating results or assisting its growth—is this not to nourish it well? When Mengzi answered Gongsun Chou’s question, he addressed this point, as though saying: The vast, flowing vital energy arises from accumulated righteousness, but is starved by righteousness seized through isolated acts. Righteousness cannot be treated as something external. Thus one must devote effort to oneself. In everything one says or does, one must govern the outward from within, making the accumulation of righteousness one’s sole concern. One must apply effort to one’s conduct and, in all dealings with others [?], use the mind to judge what is fitting, seeking only to accumulate righteousness. It is enough to keep working at this.
But if, as soon as effort begins, one expects its effects, one cannot escape seeking small gains and wanting quick results. If, as soon as work is undertaken, one calculates its completion in advance, one knows nothing of putting the difficult work first and its rewards afterward. This means that the resolve to strive in the Way [?] has been displaced by pursuit of externals, and learning through personal realization has been reduced to seeking immediate results [?]. How could this be acceptable?
Vital energy becomes full through the accumulation of righteousness. If it is not yet entirely full, the work must not cease. One should simply devote greater effort to the task and sustain it over the long term, allowing no pause even for an instant; constantly return to accumulating righteousness and sustain this through months and years, never allowing it to be forgotten even for a moment. It is enough not to forget. But if one disguises emptiness as fullness, acting artificially to assist its growth instead of letting it emerge from within, and forces weakness into strength…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
不由理勝而造作以強其充是久成之道傷於
速化自然之妙妨於襲取矣奚可哉吁有事勿
忘而戒於正助則浩然之氣得其養而無所害
矣寧有不自充乎集義養氣之節度有如此哉
嗟夫至大至剛配道義而塞天地者氣也固理
也集義之至自反常直無所愧怍則與天者游
造化在我而天下無難事矣故浩然之氣理而
已矣至於知言亦不外此理此孟子之不動心
所以非外義之告子所能彷彿也雖然浩然之
氣其迹著視太和元氣何如也此又孔孟之別
而欲學孔子者必自孟子始
===
易
善世而不伐德博而化
葛守禮
同考試官學正羅 批〔龍德正中之實作者〕
非不能言但體認欠真或以善世爲功叙乎
人或以德博爲體盛于己殊不知德與特之
分原自明白此作獨能融會傳意模寫精確
punctuated:
不由理勝而造作以強其充，是久成之道傷於速化，自然之妙妨於襲取矣，奚可哉！吁！有事勿忘，而戒於正助，則浩然之氣得其養而無所害矣，寧有不自充乎？集義養氣之節度有如此哉！嗟夫！至大至剛，配道義而塞天地者，氣也，固理也。集義之至，自反常直，無所愧怍，則與天者游，造化在我，而天下無難事矣。故浩然之氣，理而已矣。至於知言，亦不外此理。此孟子之不動心，所以非外義之告子所能彷彿也。雖然，浩然之氣，其迹著，視太和元氣何如也？此又孔孟之別，而欲學孔子者，必自孟子始。

translation_en:
…and, rather than letting principle prevail, contrive to force its fullness: this damages the way of gradual accomplishment through a demand for rapid transformation, and obstructs the subtle workings of spontaneity by trying to seize them from outside. How could this be acceptable? Ah! Attend to the work and do not forget it, while guarding against anticipating results or helping growth along. Then the vast, flowing vital force will receive nourishment without injury. How could it fail to become full of itself? Such are the proper measures for accumulating righteousness and nourishing the vital force!

Ah! That which is supremely great and supremely firm, accompanies the Way and righteousness, and fills Heaven and Earth is the vital force; it is, indeed, principle. When the accumulation of righteousness reaches its utmost, and self-examination always finds uprightness, with nothing to cause shame, one roams in company with Heaven. The processes of creation and transformation reside within oneself, and nothing in the world is difficult. Thus the vast, flowing vital force is simply principle. Understanding words likewise does not extend beyond this principle. This is why Mencius’s unperturbed mind could not be approximated by Gaozi, who regarded righteousness as external. Nevertheless, the vast, flowing vital force manifests discernible traces: how does it compare with the primordial vital force of Grand Harmony? Here, too, lies a distinction between Confucius and Mencius; yet anyone wishing to learn from Confucius must begin with Mencius.

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
殆潛心易學有得焉者宜錄以式
考試官主事陳　批　詞理精到蓋深於易學
者
考試官右給事中劉　批　簡當可式
體于己者極其純被于物者極其盛乾九二大
人然也夫善莫純於不伐施莫盛於物化也乾
九二大人以之非以德與時之兼至乎文言申
乾九二象傳之意若謂九二所以為見龍利見
者固有在於龍德正中矣夫龍德惟剛健中正
===
之備體乎立矣故自脩益密於云為存誠不懈
於無斁充滿周徧兼萬理而彌綸天下之善皆
其善也溥博淵泉舉天德而悉備世之有善皆
其有也虛己下人而韜晦為益深固曰我斯善
我之分耳而奚有於矜小心惟道而炫耀無所
事固曰我之善人所同耳而何有於夸善世不
伐如是斯體於己者其不極純矣乎正中當不
潛未躍之處時乎會矣故妙用根極于一身德
施普及乎天下風動於光輝之被無遠無近皆
punctuated:
殆潛心易學有得焉者，宜錄以式。
考試官主事陳批：詞理精到，蓋深於易學者。
考試官右給事中劉批：簡當可式。
體于己者極其純，被于物者極其盛，乾九二大人然也。夫善莫純於不伐，施莫盛於物化也。乾九二大人以之，非以德與時之兼至乎？文言申乾九二象傳之意，若謂九二所以為見龍利見者，固有在於龍德正中矣。夫龍德惟剛健中正之備，體乎立矣。故自脩益密於云為，存誠不懈於無斁。充滿周徧，兼萬理而彌綸，天下之善皆其善也；溥博淵泉，舉天德而悉備，世之有善皆其有也。虛己下人，而韜晦為益深，固曰：「我斯善，我之分耳，而奚有於矜？」小心惟道，而炫耀無所事，固曰：「我之善，人所同耳，而何有於夸？」善世不伐如是，斯體於己者其不極純矣乎？正中當不潛未躍之處，時乎會矣。故妙用根極于一身，德施普及乎天下，風動於光輝之被，無遠無近，皆

…He is presumably someone who has devoted himself to studying the Changes and gained insight into it. This should be recorded as a model.
Examiner Chen, a bureau secretary, comments: “Its language and reasoning are precise and thoroughly developed. The writer evidently has a deep understanding of the Changes.”
Examiner Liu, a supervising secretary of the Right, comments: “Concise and apt; it can serve as a model.”
What he embodies within himself reaches the utmost purity; what he extends to other beings reaches the utmost abundance. Such is the great man of the second, yang line of Qian. For goodness is purest when one does not boast of it, and beneficence is most abundant when other beings are transformed. The great man of Qian’s second, yang line puts these into practice: is this not because both his virtue and his accord with the time have reached perfection? The Commentary on the Words of the Text elaborates the meaning of the Commentary on the Images for Qian’s second, yang line. It seems to say that the reason this line signifies an appearing dragon and the benefit of seeing him assuredly lies in the dragon’s virtue being upright and central. Now, because the dragon’s virtue possesses the fullness of firmness, vigor, centrality, and correctness, its substance is established [?]. Thus his self-cultivation becomes ever more exacting in speech and action, and he preserves sincerity without slackening or weariness. Full and all-pervading, encompassing the myriad principles and comprehensively ordering them, he makes all the goodness under Heaven his own goodness. Broad and vast, deep as an abyss and flowing as a spring, he possesses the whole of Heaven’s virtue: whatever goodness exists in the world is his as well. He empties himself and places himself below others, concealing his brilliance ever more deeply. He steadfastly says: “This goodness of mine is merely my allotted duty. What is there to be proud of?” With a cautious heart intent upon the Way, he has no use for ostentation. He steadfastly says: “My goodness is shared by others. What is there to boast about?” Such is his benefiting the world without boasting. Does not what he embodies within himself thereby reach the utmost purity? Upright and central, he occupies the position of one who is no longer hidden but has not yet leapt: he has encountered the fitting time. Thus his wondrous efficacy is rooted ultimately in his own person, while his virtuous beneficence extends throughout all under Heaven. Wherever his radiance reaches, others respond as to the wind; whether far or near, all…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
其德之所囿也澤流於聲教之訖或上或下悉
其德之所漸也以心感心而潛孚莫測盖天下
文明有不知為之者正己物正而丕變無方盖
天下化成有不疾而速者德博而化如是斯被
于物者其不極盛矣乎吁九二大人之所以備
其德而際乎時者有如此此所以為見龍在田
而人所利見也歟嗟夫化者聖之至盛也其終
始亦惟一誠而已故閑邪存誠誠者也學聚問
辯寬居仁行誠之者也夫以九二之剛健中正
至德已具而猶不容已於學以成德由誠之以
至於誠斯所以善世而能化者歟觀夫子文言
前後之旨則自古聖人所以聖槩可見矣
變則通通則久
謝九儀
同考試官學正羅　批　此題以易理明治
道近時學者去九六相生之語而易之以天
地人物之變似為新見但講涉渺茫於聖人
通變宜民之道殊未為切或又泥於制器尚象
punctuated:
其德之所囿也。澤流於聲教之訖，或上或下，悉其德之所漸也。以心感心，而潛孚莫測，盖天下文明，有不知為之者；正己物正，而丕變無方，盖天下化成，有不疾而速者。德博而化如是，斯被于物者，其不極盛矣乎！吁！九二大人之所以備其德而際乎時者有如此，此所以為見龍在田而人所利見也歟！嗟夫！化者，聖之至盛也。其終始亦惟一誠而已。故閑邪存誠，誠者也；學聚問辯，寬居仁行，誠之者也。夫以九二之剛健中正，至德已具，而猶不容已於學以成德，由誠之以至於誠，斯所以善世而能化者歟！觀夫子《文言》前後之旨，則自古聖人所以聖，槩可見矣。
變則通，通則久。
謝九儀

translation_en:
…are encompassed by his virtue. His beneficence flows wherever his civilizing influence reaches; those above and those below are all permeated by his virtue. Through his heart he moves other hearts, winning their trust imperceptibly and unfathomably. Thus the world becomes enlightened without knowing who has brought this about. By rectifying himself, he rectifies all things, bringing about a great transformation without limit. Thus the world is transformed, swiftly yet without haste. When virtue is so extensive and its transforming influence so great, is not its effect upon all things supremely flourishing? Ah! Such is the way the great man of the second yang line fully develops his virtue and meets his time. Is this not why he is described as the “dragon appearing in the fields,” whom it benefits people to see? Ah! Transformation is the fullest expression of sagehood. From beginning to end, it consists solely in sincerity. Thus, warding off depravity and preserving sincerity characterize one who is sincere; accumulating learning, questioning and discriminating, dwelling in magnanimity, and acting with benevolence characterize one who makes himself sincere. With the strength and vigor, centrality and correctness of the second yang line, he already possesses consummate virtue. Yet he cannot cease learning in order to perfect that virtue. Proceeding from making himself sincere to being sincere—is this not how he brings goodness to the world and can transform it? By examining the purport of the Master's Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) throughout, we can broadly understand what has made sages sages since antiquity.

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
之事則又淺矣說理文字似此可以喚醒蒙
易者
考試官主事陳　批　明潔得旨錄之
考試官右給事中劉　批　庶幾得易理者
大傳推變通自然之利所以著聖君繼治之妙
也夫變則通通則久易理自然之利也然則聖
君之通變宜民其以此理也哉昔吾夫子之意
若謂觀黄帝堯舜之治當知隨時變通之易是
故時有消長不能拘拘於陳迹理有循環不能
===
膠膠於既往是變固生於窮矣變何以能通邪
蓋物極則有湮塞之理數窮則無圓轉之機惟
夫變以濟窮而事迹爲之一新將見湮者自是
而疏通滯者自是而流動施爲活潑無復陳迹
之泥也運用周流無復既往之塞也變其有不
通乎通固生於變矣通何以能久邪蓋人情厭
於守常事勢廢於窮蹙惟夫通生於變而機緘
爲之一闢將見推行由兹而無窮敷布由兹而
不息合天道而成憲存實經遠之規也因自然
punctuated:
之事，則又淺矣。說理文字似此，可以喚醒蒙易者。

考試官主事陳，批：明潔得旨，錄之。

考試官右給事中劉，批：庶幾得易理者。

大傳推變通自然之利，所以著聖君繼治之妙也。夫變則通，通則久，易理自然之利也。然則聖君之通變宜民，其以此理也哉！昔吾夫子之意，若謂觀黄帝、堯、舜之治，當知隨時變通之易。是故時有消長，不能拘拘於陳迹；理有循環，不能膠膠於既往。是變固生於窮矣，變何以能通邪？蓋物極則有湮塞之理，數窮則無圓轉之機。惟夫變以濟窮，而事迹爲之一新，將見湮者自是而疏通，滯者自是而流動。施爲活潑，無復陳迹之泥也；運用周流，無復既往之塞也。變其有不通乎？通固生於變矣，通何以能久邪？蓋人情厭於守常，事勢廢於窮蹙。惟夫通生於變，而機緘爲之一闢，將見推行由兹而無窮，敷布由兹而不息。合天道而成憲存，實經遠之規也；因自然
translation_en:
…such matters, then this too is shallow. Reasoned writing such as this can awaken those whose understanding of the Changes is still benighted [?].

Examiner Chen, Bureau Secretary, comments: “Clear and polished, it captures the meaning. Include it.”

Examiner Liu, Supervising Secretary of the Right, comments: “This comes close to grasping the principles of the Changes.”

The Great Commentary expounds the benefits that naturally follow from transformation and free passage, thereby revealing the subtle excellence with which sage rulers carry forward good government. Transformation brings free passage; free passage brings endurance: these are the benefits that naturally follow from the principles of the Changes. Is it not by these principles, then, that sage rulers adapt to change and act for the people's benefit? Our Master's meaning seems to have been that, in observing the government of Huangdi, Yao, and Shun, one should understand the Changes as adaptation and transformation in accordance with the times. Thus, since the times wax and wane, one cannot cling rigidly to precedents; since principle moves in cycles, one cannot remain fixed upon the past. Transformation, then, assuredly arises from exhaustion. But how can transformation bring free passage?

When things reach their utmost limit, they tend toward obstruction; when their allotted course is exhausted, there is no opportunity for smooth movement. Only through transformation that remedies exhaustion are affairs made altogether new. Then what was blocked becomes open, and what was stagnant begins to flow. Action becomes lively and vigorous, no longer mired in precedents; practical application circulates freely, no longer obstructed by the past. How could transformation fail to bring free passage? Free passage assuredly arises from transformation. But how can free passage bring endurance?

Human feelings weary of holding to the customary, and affairs fall into disuse when circumstances become straitened. Only when free passage arises from transformation are the workings of affairs opened up anew. Then implementation can proceed without limit, and extension can continue without cease. In accord with the Way of Heaven, established statutes endure: this is truly a pattern for ordering affairs for the distant future. Following what is naturally so…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
而良法寓實悠久之用也通其有不久乎夫變
而通通而久乃易理自然之利否則陰陽將滯
於形氣而非生生之妙矣然則黃帝堯舜之治
何莫非此理也哉大抵易惟陰陽變化兩端而
已在天為乾坤闔闢在易為剛柔相推在人物
為動靜相禪在聖人為隨時弛張統而言之一
易也然則黃帝堯舜垂衣裳而天下治固非聖
人所强為易為之也變通而久則流行之易又
未嘗無一定之易蓋皆出於天道之自然非知
力所能損益也學易者神而明之則易在吾心
而可與語天德王道矣
===
書
帝曰來禹汝亦昌言禹拜曰都帝予何言
吴孟祺
同考試官教諭趙　批〔此題作者類能成篇〕
〔殊多駁冗可厭校閱數日偶得此卷辭氣冲〕
〔淡制度整齊發揚盛世明良相與之氣象宛〕
〔然如見宜録之以式學者〕
punctuated:
而良法寓，實悠久之用也。通其有不久乎？夫變而通，通而久，乃易理自然之利；否則陰陽將滯於形氣，而非生生之妙矣。然則黃帝堯舜之治，何莫非此理也哉？大抵易惟陰陽變化兩端而已：在天為乾坤闔闢，在易為剛柔相推，在人物為動靜相禪，在聖人為隨時弛張。統而言之，一易也。然則黃帝堯舜垂衣裳而天下治，固非聖人所强為，易為之也。變通而久，則流行之易又未嘗無一定之易，蓋皆出於天道之自然，非知力所能損益也。學易者神而明之，則易在吾心，而可與語天德王道矣。
書
帝曰：「來，禹！汝亦昌言。」禹拜曰：「都！帝，予何言？」
吴孟祺
同考試官教諭趙　批〔此題作者類能成篇，〕〔殊多駁冗可厭。校閱數日，偶得此卷，辭氣冲〕〔淡，制度整齊，發揚盛世明良相與之氣象，宛〕〔然如見。宜録之以式學者。〕
translation_en:
…and sound methods are embodied therein: this is indeed efficacy that endures. How could free passage fail to endure? Change leading to free passage, and free passage to endurance, constitute the natural benefit of the principles of the Changes. Otherwise, yin and yang would become obstructed in physical form and vital energy, losing the subtle efficacy of ceaseless generation. Was the governance of Huangdi, Yao, and Shun anything other than this principle?
Broadly speaking, the Changes consists simply of the two aspects of yin and yang in their transformations. In Heaven, these appear as the closing and opening of Qian and Kun; in the Changes, as the firm and yielding impelling one another; in humans and other beings, as movement and stillness alternating; and in the sages, as relaxing and tightening measures according to the times. Taken together, they are one and the same Changes. Thus, when Huangdi, Yao, and Shun let their robes hang down and the world was well governed, this was certainly no forced accomplishment of the sages: the Changes brought it about. Through change and free passage comes endurance; thus, within the Changes in its flowing operation there is always also the Changes in its fixed constancy. All of this arises from the spontaneity of the Way of Heaven; human intelligence and effort can neither diminish nor augment it. When students of the Changes comprehend it with spiritual insight, the Changes resides in their own hearts, and one may discuss with them the virtue of Heaven and the Way of kings.
Book of Documents
The emperor said: “Come, Yu! You too should offer excellent counsel.” Yu bowed and said: “Ah! O Emperor, what can I say?”
Wu Mengqi
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Those writing on this topic can generally produce a complete essay, but all too many are tiresomely inconsistent and prolix. After several days of reading and assessing, I happened upon this script. Its language and tone are serene and unadorned, its structure orderly. It brings forth the atmosphere of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers working together in a flourishing age, so vividly that one seems to see them. It should be recorded to serve as a model for students.”

聖君進大臣而求善也切大臣復聖君而遜善
也恭甚矣虞廷君臣以善相師者也一呼復問
答之間而求善遜善之美具焉史臣紀之有以
===

考試官主事陳批〔莊重精切，逈異諸作。〕
考試官右給事中劉批〔意在言外，此作得之。〕
聖君進大臣而求善也切，大臣復聖君而遜善也恭。甚矣，虞廷君臣以善相師者也！一呼復問答之間，而求善遜善之美具焉。史臣紀之，有以哉！昔帝舜既聞謨于皐陶，遂求益於大禹，乃曰「來」以招致其進，曰「禹」以特表其名。遵侍在廷，將以顧夫問也。且謂：「納言當集夫衆善，嘉猷豈厭於再聞？如皐陶者，知人之哲既爲朕詳敷於前，安民之惠復爲朕開導於後。汝始則固以爲難，而終則深以爲信者矣。然人各有見，事非一端，顧肯言及之而不言乎？亦必廣責難之敬，以昌言而續告之，于以反復詳敷，推其未盡之旨；委曲開導，恊夫同寅之公。予其試聽哉！」帝舜求言
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔“The flourishing relationship between an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers under Youyu is exceedingly difficult to describe. This composition vividly and aptly portrays the sincerity with which the great Shun sought good counsel and the admirable modesty with which the great Yu deferred to others’ excellence. It enables us to envision events several thousand years in the past.”〕 An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!
Examiner Chen, Secretary, comments: 〔“Dignified, precise, and incisive; markedly different from the other compositions.”〕
Examiner Liu, Right Supervising Secretary, comments: 〔“The meaning lies beyond the words; this composition captures it.”〕
The sage ruler summoned his great minister forward with an earnest desire for good counsel; the great minister answered his sage ruler with reverent modesty, yielding credit for excellence to others. How profoundly the ruler and ministers at the court of Yu taught one another through goodness! In a single exchange of summons, response, question, and answer [?], the admirable qualities of seeking good counsel and modestly deferring to others’ excellence were fully present. The court historian had good reason to record it!
In former times, Emperor Shun, having heard Gao Yao’s counsels, sought further benefit from the great Yu. He said “Come,” summoning him to advance, and “Yu,” singling him out by name. Yu stood in attendance at court, awaiting the ruler’s inquiry [?]. Shun’s meaning was moreover this: “In receiving counsel, one should gather all that is good from everyone. How could one tire of hearing excellent plans again? Gao Yao has already expounded to me in detail the wisdom required to understand men, and then further instructed me in the beneficence required to bring peace to the people. At first you indeed considered these things difficult, but in the end you deeply affirmed his words as true. Yet each person has his own insights, and affairs have more than one aspect. Would you be willing to address these matters, yet leave something unsaid? You must further extend the reverence expressed by holding your ruler to demanding standards, continuing to instruct me with excellent words. Through repeated and detailed exposition, develop the implications he has not exhausted; through thorough and painstaking instruction, accord with the impartial spirit of colleagues united in reverence. Let me hear what you have to say!” Emperor Shun’s desire to hear counsel…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
之意其切如此禹方承命于帝不覺競惕於中
乃拜手以盡其禮都美以發於嘆又稱曰帝所
以啓其聽也且謂進忠不在於多言用言惟求
夫至當使臯陶者徒曰知人而功效有所未明
但曰安民而究極有所未備揆之於理而未順
措之於事而難行予固當更竭祗承之慮仰裨
重華之助可也今彼之所言如出一口非得我
心之同然乎予雖欲效臣隣之義以輔翼而分
責之彼則語焉懇到不惟順理而且可行謨焉
精至不惟可行而且底績予復何所言哉大禹
===
復君之辭其謙如此是則君不自聖而求言於
臣臣不自居而讓善於同列上下以誠交孚可
以想見有虞之盛歟抑禹欲無言豈終於無言
哉禹之心蓋以言有難繼惟思孜孜述其治水
之功相與保守不怠是言之昌莫大於此臯陶
亦俞而師之舜之心惟恐闢有未盡而取善無
窮圖治不已者也是言之昌終亦無弗闢者意
舜禹聖之盛也唐虞治之極也君臣猶不自足
punctuated: 之意，其切如此。禹方承命于帝，不覺競惕於中，乃拜手以盡其禮，都美以發於嘆，又稱曰「帝」，所以啓其聽也。且謂進忠不在於多言，用言惟求夫至當。使臯陶者徒曰知人，而功效有所未明；但曰安民，而究極有所未備；揆之於理而未順，措之於事而難行，予固當更竭祗承之慮，仰裨重華之助可也。今彼之所言，如出一口，非得我心之同然乎？予雖欲效臣隣之義，以輔翼而分責之，彼則語焉懇到，不惟順理而且可行；謨焉精至，不惟可行而且底績。予復何所言哉？大禹復君之辭，其謙如此。是則君不自聖而求言於臣，臣不自居而讓善於同列，上下以誠交孚，可以想見有虞之盛歟！抑禹欲無言，豈終於無言哉？禹之心，蓋以言有難繼，惟思孜孜，述其治水之功，相與保守不怠，是言之昌莫大於此，臯陶亦俞而師之。舜之心，惟恐闢有未盡，而取善無窮、圖治不已者也，是言之昌，終亦無弗闢者。意！舜禹，聖之盛也；唐虞，治之極也。君臣猶不自足，
translation_en:
…such was the earnestness of his desire to seek counsel. As Yu received the emperor’s command, he could not help feeling apprehensive and vigilant within. He bowed with his hands joined to fulfill the requirements of ceremony, voiced his admiration in the exclamation “Du!”, and then addressed him as “Emperor,” to invite his attention. His meaning was this: “Offering loyal counsel does not depend on speaking at length; in employing words, one seeks only what is entirely fitting. Had Gao Yao merely spoken of discerning men’s abilities without making the resulting achievements clear, or merely spoken of bringing peace to the people without fully exploring the matter; had his counsel failed to accord with principle when measured against it, or proved difficult to implement when applied to affairs, then I certainly ought to exert myself further in considering how reverently to carry out my charge and offer assistance to Chonghua [Shun]. But now his words are as though spoken from our common mouth: do they not express what my own heart likewise approves? Although I wish to fulfill my duty as a minister close to the ruler, assisting him and sharing his responsibilities, Gao Yao’s words are earnest and thorough, both consistent with principle and practicable; his plans are precise and consummate, both practicable and capable of producing results. What more could I say?” Such was the humility of the Great Yu’s reply to his ruler.

Thus the ruler did not regard himself as a sage but sought counsel from his ministers; the minister did not claim credit for himself but yielded it to his colleagues. Those above and below trusted one another in sincerity. Can we not picture from this the flourishing age of Youyu [Shun]? Yet although Yu wished to say nothing, did he remain silent to the end? Yu felt that such words were difficult to follow, and thought only of diligent effort. He recounted his achievements in controlling the waters, so that together they might preserve them without slackening. No excellent counsel could surpass this; Gao Yao too assented and took it as his guide. Shun, for his part, feared only that he had not yet opened himself fully to counsel; he accepted good advice without limit and pursued good government without cease. Such excellent counsel would, in the end, always find him receptive.

Ah [?]! Shun and Yu represented the highest flourishing of sagehood; the ages of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] marked the utmost perfection of government. Yet ruler and ministers alike remained unsatisfied with themselves…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
其視後世治僅小康君驕而臣諛者亦獨何哉
惟曰欲至于萬年惟王子子孫孫永保民
盧宗哲
同考試官教諭趙　批　命題本意正欲寫出
周臣忠愛之心此篇精明條暢發揚殆盡故
錄
同考試官教諭王　批　題本平易士子多于
惟欲二字體認欠真故措辭漫無源委此篇
會文切理其亦忠愛之心溢于言表者乎
考試官主事陳　批　得古人告君意而文亦
===
敷暢
考試官右給事中劉　批　詞暢意足可錄
周臣表進戒之心惟祈君永膺天命而世保天
下也甚矣天命永于有德也人臣以永命祝望
其君忠愛之誠至矣史官紀周臣進戒之詞至
此蓋謂君道在於得天而得天本乎明德我
啓王監祖德以懷諸侯而化迷民者豈有他哉
亦惟為王祈天永命而已何則誕受多方周之
punctuated:
其視後世治僅小康、君驕而臣諛者，亦獨何哉？

惟曰欲至于萬年，惟王子子孫孫永保民。
盧宗哲

同考試官教諭趙批：命題本意，正欲寫出周臣忠愛之心。此篇精明條暢，發揚殆盡，故錄。

同考試官教諭王批：題本平易，士子多于「惟欲」二字體認欠真，故措辭漫無源委。此篇會文切理，其亦忠愛之心溢于言表者乎？

考試官主事陳批：得古人告君意，而文亦敷暢。

考試官右給事中劉批：詞暢意足，可錄。

周臣表進戒之心，惟祈君永膺天命而世保天下也。甚矣，天命永于有德也！人臣以永命祝望其君，忠愛之誠至矣！史官紀周臣進戒之詞，至此蓋謂君道在於得天，而得天本乎明德。我啓王監祖德，以懷諸侯而化迷民者，豈有他哉？亦惟為王祈天永命而已。何則？誕受多方，周之
translation_en:
…How does this compare with later ages, when government achieved only modest peace, while rulers were arrogant and ministers sycophantic? Why indeed were they so different?

“Desiring only that it extend to ten thousand years, and that the king’s sons and grandsons forever protect the people.”
Lu Zongzhe

Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: The purpose of setting this topic was precisely to bring out the Zhou minister’s loyal devotion. This essay is clear, discerning, well ordered, and fluent; it develops that meaning almost exhaustively. Hence its selection.

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: The topic is straightforward, but most candidates fail to grasp truly the two characters meaning “only desire”; consequently, their wording rambles without tracing the thought’s origin and development. This essay grasps the text and accords closely with its principles. Does not a heart of loyal devotion overflow beyond its words?

Examiner Chen, Secretary, comments: It captures the spirit in which the ancients counseled their rulers, and its prose is also expansive and fluent.

Examiner Liu, Supervising Secretary of the Right, comments: Fluent in expression and full in meaning; worthy of selection.

The Zhou minister expressed his purpose in offering admonition: he prayed only that his ruler might forever receive Heaven’s Mandate and preserve possession of All under Heaven through successive generations. How enduring indeed is Heaven’s Mandate for those who possess virtue! When a minister prays and hopes that his ruler’s mandate will endure, the sincerity of his loyal devotion reaches its utmost. In recording the Zhou minister’s words of admonition, the historian here presumably means that the way of the ruler lies in winning Heaven’s favor, and that winning Heaven’s favor rests upon manifesting virtue. “In urging the king to take his ancestors’ virtue as his mirror, thereby winning over the feudal lords and transforming the misguided people, could I have any other purpose? I seek only to pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate for the king.” Why is this so? In receiving the many regions on so grand a scale, Zhou’s…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
荷天寵也厚矣然眷命難乎其有終惟欲無疆
之寵自今引之至于萬年而益隆撫臨兆民周
之荷天休也渥矣然王業必傳于悠久惟欲滋
至之休自今延之至于無窮而罔替可大之基
積而為可久之祚非如夏之歷年而已也而六
服群辟永作周家之藩屏繼統之善衍而為垂
統之澤非若商之歷年而止也而群黎百姓恒
屬周家之版圖由是繼王之身有子焉子而復
子嗣大歷服以永保乎庶邦之衆繼王之子有
===
孫焉孫而又孫並受丕基以永綏乎中國之民
世德作求綿綿乎專美一姓而時叙修和之績
終無不競之虞也所謂宜君宜王者有焉繩其
祖武振振乎克紹前烈而奠麗陳教之光靡有
過佚之失也所謂惟乃世王者有焉夫然則臣
下祝望之心以慰而吾王用德之效端在是矣
抑論皇天無親惟德是輔欲得天者誠不可不
脩德也夫德徵於民而天命不在民心外也故
周之大臣祝君永命必以民先之為之君者果
punctuated:
荷天寵也厚矣，然眷命難乎其有終，惟欲無疆之寵自今引之，至于萬年而益隆。撫臨兆民，周之荷天休也渥矣，然王業必傳于悠久，惟欲滋至之休自今延之，至于無窮而罔替。可大之基積而為可久之祚，非如夏之歷年而已也，而六服群辟永作周家之藩屏；繼統之善衍而為垂統之澤，非若商之歷年而止也，而群黎百姓恒屬周家之版圖。由是繼王之身有子焉，子而復子，嗣大歷服，以永保乎庶邦之衆；繼王之子有孫焉，孫而又孫，並受丕基，以永綏乎中國之民。世德作求，綿綿乎專美一姓，而時叙修和之績終無不競之虞也，所謂「宜君宜王」者有焉；繩其祖武，振振乎克紹前烈，而奠麗陳教之光靡有過佚之失也，所謂「惟乃世王」者有焉。夫然則臣下祝望之心以慰，而吾王用德之效端在是矣。

抑論皇天無親，惟德是輔，欲得天者誠不可不脩德也。夫德徵於民，而天命不在民心外也，故周之大臣祝君永命，必以民先之。為之君者果
translation_en:
…Zhou has received Heaven’s favor in abundance. Yet it is difficult to retain Heaven’s gracious mandate to the end; their sole wish is that this boundless favor may henceforth extend for ten thousand years and grow still greater. In presiding over the myriad people, Zhou has received Heaven’s blessings most generously. Yet the royal enterprise must be transmitted into the distant future; their sole wish is that these ever-increasing blessings may henceforth continue without limit and never decline. A foundation capable of greatness will, through accumulation, become a dynastic inheritance capable of enduring. Its span will not merely equal the years of Xia: the many lords of the six zones of service will forever serve as Zhou’s protective bulwarks. The excellence of succeeding to the royal line will expand into blessings bequeathed to future successors. Its span will not stop at the years attained by Shang: the common people will remain forever within Zhou’s registered domains. Thus the king himself will be succeeded by sons, and sons in turn by sons, inheriting the great and enduring royal charge and forever protecting the multitudes of the many states. The king’s sons will be succeeded by grandsons, and grandsons in turn by grandsons, all receiving the great foundation and forever bringing peace to the people of the central realm. Seeking to continue the virtue of successive generations, they will perpetually concentrate this glory in a single ruling house. Their achievements in duly ordering affairs and cultivating harmony will never be threatened by weakness. Here will be realized the saying, “Fit to be a lord, fit to be a king.” Following their ancestors’ footsteps, flourishing generations will carry on their predecessors’ glorious deeds. Their splendid work of settling the people, securing their allegiance, and setting forth instruction will be free of the failings of excess and indolence. Here will be realized the saying, “Then your descendants shall reign through the generations.” In this way the hopes and prayers of the ministers will be fulfilled, and precisely herein will lie the results of our king’s exercise of virtue.

Moreover, August Heaven shows no partiality; it supports virtue alone. Anyone who wishes to gain Heaven’s favor must indeed cultivate virtue. Virtue is manifested among the people, and Heaven’s mandate does not exist apart from their hearts. Thus, when Zhou’s great ministers prayed that their ruler might retain the mandate forever, they invariably put the people first. If their ruler truly …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
能以德誠民則民心永懐而天命自有不庸釋
焉者矣周祚八百年之永者豈偶然哉噫斯祝
也頌而無諂信非周召之徒不能為矣大臣愛
君者尚其監之
詩
樂只君子民之父母樂只君子德音不已
李開先

同考試官教諭胡　批〔布置齊整而語致從容自是作家手段〕
===
考試官主事陳　批〔詞氣從容非苟作者〕
考試官右給事中劉　批〔得古人尊賓之意〕
主人美嘉賓之德有為人所依者有為人所傳
者盖德為民之所依則其譽自可傳也賔之可
樂孰有大於是哉主人美之以致尊之之意宜
矣此周人燕饗通用之樂盖假工歌以道達主
人之意若謂德以長人為尊譽以垂世為美令
punctuated:
能以德誠民，則民心永懐，而天命自有不庸釋焉者矣。周祚八百年之永者，豈偶然哉？噫！斯祝也，頌而無諂，信非周召之徒不能為矣。大臣愛君者，尚其監之。
詩
樂只君子，民之父母；樂只君子，德音不已。
