Can this be right? The Gongyang and Guliang commentaries each have their strengths and failings, but the two masters Jiang and Hu each specialized in one canonical tradition and rejected the other. Could there ultimately have been no judgment reconciling them? Gaotang Sheng transmitted seventeen chapters of the Rites of the Servicemen, while the fifty-six chapters obtained by Prince Xian of Hejian also included rites for the Son of Heaven and the feudal lords. Yet these were all set aside without study, and scholars merely extrapolated from the rites of servicemen to arrive at those of the Son of Heaven, preventing the world and later generations from seeing the sages’ complete canon. Is this not profoundly regrettable? In general, the Han scholars were meticulous in explaining words but cursory concerning the great principles, skilled in textual investigation but unable to grasp the connections…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
通故其學雖有淺深之殊要皆不免穿鑿
附會之失王通氏曰九師興而易道微三
傳作而春秋散齊魯毛韓詩之末也大戴
小戴禮之衰也而鄭夾漈氏亦曰秦人焚
書而書存諸儒窮經而經絕者良有以也
今觀其致用也申公能對力行之一言而
乃汲汲於明堂巡狩之事夏侯能明皇極
之大旨而反垂意於青紫之得說詩解頤
能陳關雎之義矣然政龐有漸卒無三百
===
篇敢諫之風此衡之所以異於王式也由
學有戒能明湯武之心矣然賢良見微竟
以老而罷歸此固之所以異於伏生也梁
丘賀圖形麒麟而實以筮應得幸兒寬以
循良課最而贊成封禪之事歐陽歙八世
傳書教授千餘人而終不救多贓之敗君
子皆有所不滿焉者蓋至是而諸儒之優
劣得失見矣嗚呼經以致用用必通經施
之用者既如彼則其得之經者可知矣況
punctuated:
通，故其學雖有淺深之殊，要皆不免穿鑿附會之失。王通氏曰：「九師興而易道微，三傳作而春秋散，齊魯毛韓，詩之末也；大戴小戴，禮之衰也。」而鄭夾漈氏亦曰：「秦人焚書而書存，諸儒窮經而經絕。」者良有以也。
今觀其致用也，申公能對力行之一言，而乃汲汲於明堂巡狩之事；夏侯能明皇極之大旨，而反垂意於青紫之得。說詩解頤，能陳關雎之義矣，然政龐有漸，卒無三百篇敢諫之風，此衡之所以異於王式也。由學有戒，能明湯武之心矣，然賢良見微，竟以老而罷歸，此固之所以異於伏生也。梁丘賀圖形麒麟，而實以筮應得幸；兒寬以循良課最，而贊成封禪之事；歐陽歙八世傳書，教授千餘人，而終不救多贓之敗。君子皆有所不滿焉者，蓋至是而諸儒之優劣得失見矣。
嗚呼！經以致用，用必通經。施之用者既如彼，則其得之經者可知矣。況
translation_en:
…comprehensive understanding. Thus, although their learning differed in depth, all were ultimately subject to the faults of strained interpretation and forced connections. Wang Tong said: “When the Nine Masters arose, the Way of the Changes declined; when the Three Commentaries appeared, the Spring and Autumn Annals became fragmented. The Qi, Lu, Mao, and Han traditions represent the latter stages of the Odes; the Elder Dai and Younger Dai represent the decline of the Rites.” Zheng Jiaji likewise said: “The men of Qin burned the books, yet the books survived; the Confucian scholars exhaustively studied the Classics, yet the Classics were cut off.” There were sound reasons for these statements.
Now consider how they put their learning into practice. Master Shen could offer the single counsel of earnest practice, yet busied himself with the Hall of Light and imperial inspection tours. Xiahou could elucidate the central meaning of the “Sovereign’s Standard,” yet turned his attention to obtaining the blue and purple insignia of office. His explanations of the Odes made listeners smile with delight, and he could expound the meaning of “The Ospreys”; yet, as disorder in government gradually developed [?], he ultimately lacked the spirit of bold remonstrance embodied in the three hundred poems. This is what distinguished Heng (Kuang Heng) from Wang Shi. “Through study there is admonition” [?]: he could clarify the intentions of Tang and Wu; yet, when recommended as Worthy and Good, he perceived subtle signs [?] and was eventually dismissed and sent home on grounds of age. This is what distinguished Gu (Yuan Gu) from Master Fu. Liangqiu He had his portrait displayed in the Qilin Pavilion, but in fact gained imperial favor through successful divination with milfoil. Ni Kuan received the highest performance assessment for benevolent administration, yet supported the undertaking of the Feng and Shan sacrifices. Ouyang Xi, whose family had transmitted the Documents for eight generations, taught more than a thousand people, yet ultimately could not avert his downfall through extensive corruption. In all these men, the gentleman finds grounds for dissatisfaction. Here, indeed, the strengths and weaknesses, successes and failures of these scholars become apparent.
Alas! The Classics are for practical application, and practical application requires a comprehensive understanding of the Classics. Since their application was as described above, we can infer what they had gained from the Classics. How much less, then, …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
望其得斯道之傳哉雖然諸儒之功亦未
可盡泯也夫當典籍旣厄經生解散使傳
註之書不作師友之學不講則殘編斷簡
人誰知經而後人雖欲因經以考傳之得
失因傳以究經之本原亦將無所依據矣
中間歷漢及唐千餘年而吾道一綫之緒
尚賴不墜者固諸儒維持之力耳宋興眞
儒輩出程子得不傳之學於遺經朱子集
諸儒之大成程作易傳朱作本義而易之
===
道明矣蔡沈以朱子之意作書傳而書之
道明矣朱子作詩經集傳而自謂可無遺
憾作儀禮集解而自謂於世有補而春秋
則又程子胡安國相繼為之發明而表章
之而六經之學煥然大明於世矣然非漢
儒開其源則宋儒何以導其流哉故曰漢
儒之功殆未盡泯也然則後之學者當何
學亦曰漢儒其粗也宋儒其精也漢儒得
其迹而宋儒得其心也由其粗以達其精
punctuated: 望其得斯道之傳哉？雖然，諸儒之功亦未可盡泯也。夫當典籍旣厄，經生解散，使傳註之書不作，師友之學不講，則殘編斷簡，人誰知經？而後人雖欲因經以考傳之得失，因傳以究經之本原，亦將無所依據矣。中間歷漢及唐千餘年，而吾道一綫之緒尚賴不墜者，固諸儒維持之力耳。宋興，眞儒輩出，程子得不傳之學於遺經，朱子集諸儒之大成。程作《易傳》，朱作《本義》，而《易》之道明矣。蔡沈以朱子之意作《書傳》，而《書》之道明矣。朱子作《詩經集傳》，而自謂可無遺憾；作《儀禮集解》，而自謂於世有補。而《春秋》，則又程子、胡安國相繼為之發明而表章之，而六經之學煥然大明於世矣。然非漢儒開其源，則宋儒何以導其流哉？故曰漢儒之功殆未盡泯也。然則後之學者當何學？亦曰漢儒其粗也，宋儒其精也；漢儒得其迹，而宋儒得其心也。由其粗以達其精
translation_en:
…expect them to have received the transmission of this Way? Even so, the contributions of these scholars cannot be wholly effaced. When the canonical writings had suffered calamity and students of the classics had dispersed, had books of commentary not been written and learning among teachers and friends not been pursued, who could have understood the classics from their broken chapters and fragmentary slips? Even if later generations wished to use the classics to assess the merits and faults of the commentaries, and the commentaries to investigate the fundamental meaning of the classics, they would have had nothing on which to rely. Throughout the more than a thousand years spanning the Han and Tang dynasties, the slender thread of our Way remained unbroken precisely through these scholars’ efforts to preserve it.
With the rise of the Song, true Confucian scholars appeared in succession. Master Cheng recovered from the surviving classics the learning whose transmission had been lost, and Master Zhu brought together the achievements of the various scholars. Cheng composed the Commentary on the Changes, and Zhu the Original Meaning of the Changes, and thus the Way of the Book of Changes became clear. Following Master Zhu’s intentions, Cai Shen composed the Commentary on the Documents, and thus the Way of the Book of Documents became clear. Master Zhu composed the Collected Commentaries on the Book of Odes and declared that he could have no remaining regrets; he composed the Collected Explanations of the Ceremonies and Rites [?] and declared that it would benefit the world. As for the Spring and Autumn Annals, Master Cheng and Hu Anguo successively elucidated and brought its meaning to prominence. Thus the learning of the Six Classics shone forth brilliantly in the world.
Yet had the Han scholars not opened the source, how could the Song scholars have guided its flow? Thus I say that the contributions of the Han scholars surely cannot be wholly effaced. What, then, should later students study? One may say that the Han scholars represent its rudiments and the Song scholars its essentials; the Han scholars grasped its outward traces, while the Song scholars grasped its heart. By proceeding from its rudiments to reach its essentials…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
因其迹以求其心則顏曾思孟之學可幾
而夫子六經之旨不在六經而在吾心矣
聖何人哉希之則是執事其以爲何如
第三問
楊獻可
同考試官教諭趙　批〔本房善苓者頗多而考據詳明殆無踰子者宜錄以式〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔是策正觀諸士考古之學而子能備陳之可以占子之蘊矣〕
考試官主事陳　批〔儀禮之書士多忽而不講是篇考據精詳條荅無遺殆究心禮學而有得者〕
===
考試官右給事中劉　批〔策對知禮可取〕
考古人之禮而推其全得古人之意而措
諸禮斯學不謬而用不窒矣夫不推其全
則古人制作之義未明而或至於謬不得
其意則今日事勢之權不合而或至於迂
是故有引伸觸類之學而又有隨時變通
punctuated:
因其迹以求其心，則顏、曾、思、孟之學可幾，而夫子六經之旨不在六經而在吾心矣。聖何人哉？希之則是。執事其以爲何如？

第三問
楊獻可
同考試官教諭趙　批〔本房善苓者頗多，而考據詳明，殆無踰子者，宜錄以式。〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔是策正觀諸士考古之學，而子能備陳之，可以占子之蘊矣。〕
考試官主事陳　批〔儀禮之書，士多忽而不講。是篇考據精詳，條荅無遺，殆究心禮學而有得者。〕
考試官右給事中劉　批〔策對知禮，可取。〕

考古人之禮而推其全，得古人之意而措諸禮，斯學不謬而用不窒矣。夫不推其全，則古人制作之義未明，而或至於謬；不得其意，則今日事勢之權不合，而或至於迂。是故有引伸觸類之學，而又有隨時變通
translation_en:
…By following their outward traces to seek their inner meaning, one may approach the learning of Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, Zisi, and Mengzi; then the Master's purport in the Six Classics will reside not in the Six Classics but in one's own heart. What sort of person is a sage? Aspire to be one, and you can become one. What do you, honored examiners, think of this?

Third Question
Yang Xianke

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: 〔There are quite a few accomplished candidates [?] in this examining section, but scarcely anyone surpasses you in the thoroughness and clarity of textual substantiation. This should be selected as a model.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔This policy question is precisely intended to assess the candidates' learning in the study of antiquity. Your ability to set it out fully allows us to discern the depth of your learning.〕

Comment by Examiner Chen, Secretary: 〔Candidates often neglect the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) and fail to study it. This essay is precise and thorough in its textual substantiation and answers each point without omission. Its author has evidently devoted himself to the study of ritual and gained understanding.〕

Comment by Examiner Liu, Supervising Secretary of the Right: 〔This policy answer demonstrates knowledge of ritual and merits selection.〕

By examining the rites of the ancients and extending one's inquiry to their entirety, grasping the ancients' intent and giving it expression in ritual, one's learning will be free from error and its application unobstructed. If one does not investigate their entirety, the principles underlying the ancients' institutions remain unclear, and one may fall into error. If one does not grasp their intent, one's judgments will fail to accord with present circumstances, and one may become impractical. Thus there must be learning that extends implications and draws analogies, together with adaptation to changing times…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
之宜則古人制作庶可以會其全而雖今
日所行之稍異亦固得其意於千載之下
矣請敬陳之昔者周家監二代而文天下
之治天下安於禮而周公紀之於書此儀
禮之經所由傳也秦火之後所存無幾蓋
得之高堂生者僅十七篇鄭玄註之賈公
彥䟽之至今存焉有志於古者其能舍是
不講乎以覲禮言之侯氏至郊則有勞有
賜舍有戒其朝有奠圭有享天子有車服
===
之賜此其槩矣然上公之圭冕車牢饗獻
食舉皆以九數朝位九十步擯者五人三
問三勞諸侯視公殺其二其擯與問勞殺
其一諸伯如侯而子男又殺焉若是者皆
載於周禮大行人而儀禮正言覲禮不之
及者蓋周制有春朝秋覲夏宗冬遇朝宗
禮備覲遇禮省圭冕諸物之數意必備載
於朝宗之篇而今亡矣幸而有周禮之存
也斯堂陛分嚴君臣情通因斯以推乎朝
punctuated:
之宜，則古人制作庶可以會其全，而雖今日所行之稍異，亦固得其意於千載之下矣。請敬陳之。昔者周家監二代而文天下之治，天下安於禮，而周公紀之於書，此《儀禮》之經所由傳也。秦火之後，所存無幾，蓋得之高堂生者僅十七篇，鄭玄註之，賈公彥䟽之，至今存焉。有志於古者，其能舍是不講乎？
以《覲禮》言之，侯氏至郊，則有勞，有賜舍，有戒；其朝有奠圭，有享天子，有車服之賜，此其槩矣。然上公之圭、冕、車、牢、饗、獻、食、舉，皆以九數，朝位九十步，擯者五人，三問三勞。諸侯視公殺其二，其擯與問勞殺其一；諸伯如侯，而子男又殺焉。若是者，皆載於《周禮》大行人，而《儀禮》正言覲禮不之及者，蓋周制有春朝、秋覲、夏宗、冬遇，朝宗禮備，覲遇禮省。圭冕諸物之數，意必備載於朝宗之篇，而今亡矣。幸而有《周禮》之存也，斯堂陛分嚴，君臣情通，因斯以推乎朝
translation_en:
…and the appropriateness of adapting to changing circumstances, then we may hope to comprehend the institutions of the ancients in their entirety. Even if present-day practices differ somewhat, we may still grasp their intent a thousand years later. Allow me respectfully to set this forth. In former times, the Zhou dynasty took the two preceding dynasties as its models and embellished the governance of the realm with cultural forms. All under Heaven found security in ritual, and the Duke of Zhou recorded it in writing. This is how the canonical text of the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) came to be transmitted. After the Qin book burning, little survived: only seventeen chapters were recovered from Gaotang Sheng. Zheng Xuan annotated them, and Jia Gongyan wrote a subcommentary; they survive to this day. Could anyone devoted to antiquity set this work aside without studying it?
To take the chapter “Audience with the Son of Heaven” as an example: when a lord reaches the outskirts of the capital, he receives a formal welcome, is assigned lodging, and is given instructions. At his audience, he lays down his jade tablet, presents offerings to the Son of Heaven, and receives gifts of carriages and ceremonial robes. Such is the broad outline. Yet for a duke of the highest rank, the jade tablet, ceremonial cap, carriages, sets of sacrificial animals, banquets, presentations of wine, meals, and accompanying musical performances all follow the number nine. His audience position is ninety paces away; five ushers attend him; and he receives three inquiries and three formal welcomes. For marquises, the numbers prescribed for dukes are reduced by two, while the number of ushers, inquiries, and welcomes is reduced by one. Earls follow the same provisions as marquises, while those for viscounts and barons are reduced further. Such provisions are all recorded in the section on the Chief Usher in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). The reason the Ceremonies and Rites, though expressly discussing the autumn audience, does not cover them is that the Zhou system distinguished the spring audience, autumn audience, summer audience, and winter audience. The spring and summer audiences had a full complement of rites; those of autumn and winter had abbreviated rites. Presumably, the prescribed numbers for jade tablets, ceremonial caps, and other objects were fully recorded in the chapters on the spring and summer audiences, which are now lost. Fortunately, the Rites of Zhou survives. Thus the distinctions between ruler and subject, represented by the hall and its steps, remain strict, while their sentiments find mutual expression. From this we may infer the rites of the spring audience…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
宗諸禮可矣是豈徒在於儀章物采之云
乎以少牢饋食之禮言之諸侯之卿大夫
之祭鼎俎尊罍豆籩之屬有序迎尸有節
羞獻有次主人主婦尸祝賓佐交獻有儀
利成尸謖而養嘏斯舉禮亦備矣然復筵
於尸西迎尸拜至若獻薦羞酢主人獻賓
於酬尸之後獻兄弟於酬長賓之後乃獻
內賓獻私人而三獻作爵後之獻酬以次
而舉焉若是者别載於下篇即所謂有司
===
徹者是已蓋以不儐尸則徹饋饌于室中
西北隅以為陽厭儐尸則無西北隅之饌
而此薦俎之陳有祭象而亦有陽厭之義
孝子心乎神之所在而庶其厭飫於此且
以備獻酬之禮洽兄弟之歡也此事死如
生事亡如存因斯禮以參乎特牲饋食及
所缺諸篇可也是奚可滯於器數薦獻之
節乎昏禮載於經而記有昏義合而考之
對筵合巹所以合體同尊卑以親之也贊
punctuated:
宗諸禮可矣。是豈徒在於儀章物采之云乎？以少牢饋食之禮言之，諸侯之卿大夫之祭，鼎俎尊罍豆籩之屬有序，迎尸有節，羞獻有次，主人主婦尸祝賓佐交獻有儀，利成尸謖，而養嘏斯舉，禮亦備矣。然復筵於尸西，迎尸拜至，若獻薦羞酢主人，獻賓於酬尸之後，獻兄弟於酬長賓之後，乃獻內賓、獻私人，而三獻作爵，後之獻酬以次而舉焉。若是者别載於下篇，即所謂《有司徹》者是已。蓋以不儐尸，則徹饋饌于室中西北隅，以為陽厭；儐尸，則無西北隅之饌，而此薦俎之陳，有祭象而亦有陽厭之義。孝子心乎神之所在，而庶其厭飫於此，且以備獻酬之禮，洽兄弟之歡也。此事死如生，事亡如存，因斯禮以參乎《特牲饋食》及所缺諸篇可也。是奚可滯於器數薦獻之節乎？
昏禮載於經，而記有《昏義》，合而考之，對筵合巹，所以合體、同尊卑以親之也。贊
translation_en:
…and the other rites of zong audiences may thus be inferred. Could their significance lie merely in ceremonial forms and the adornment of objects?
Consider the rite of presenting food with the lesser animal offering. In sacrifices performed by ministers and grand masters of the feudal lords, the tripods, meat stands, wine vessels, jars, dishes, and baskets are arranged in order. Welcoming the impersonator of the deceased follows prescribed forms; presenting foods and offerings follows a sequence. There are prescribed forms for the exchanges of offerings among the host, the hostess, the impersonator, the invocator, the guests, and the assistants. The completion of the service is announced, the impersonator rises, and nourishment and blessings are bestowed [?]. The rite is already complete.
Yet mats are then laid out to the west of the impersonator’s place, and he is welcomed and greeted with bows upon his arrival. Such acts as presenting wine and foods and returning a cup to the host follow. The host presents wine to the guests after offering a reciprocal cup to the impersonator, and to his kinsmen after offering a reciprocal cup to the senior guest. He then presents wine to the female guests and to his retainers. The third presenter raises the cup, and the subsequent presentations and reciprocal offerings proceed in sequence. These matters are recorded separately in the following chapter, namely, “The Attendants Clear Away the Offerings.”
When the impersonator is not entertained as a guest, the sacrificial foods are removed to the northwestern corner of the chamber to constitute the yangyan, the offering for the spirit’s unseen enjoyment in the light. When the impersonator is entertained as a guest, no foods are placed in that corner. The foods and meat stands displayed on this occasion have the appearance of a sacrifice and also carry the meaning of the yangyan. The filial son directs his heart toward wherever the spirit may be, hoping that it will eat its fill here. At the same time, he completes the rites of presenting and reciprocating cups and brings his kinsmen together in shared enjoyment. This is to serve the dead as one serves the living, and to serve the departed as though they were present. This rite may therefore be used to illuminate “Presenting Food with a Single Animal Offering” and the missing chapters. How could one remain confined to the prescribed numbers of vessels and the procedures for presenting foods and offerings?
The wedding rite is recorded in the classic, while the Record of Rites contains “The Meaning of the Wedding Rite.” Examining them together shows that facing one another on their mats and drinking from the paired halves of a gourd serve to unite the couple as one body, give them equal standing, and bring them into intimacy. The ritual assistant…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
見婦於舅姑婦執笲棗栗腶脩升自西階
以見贊醴婦婦祭脯醢祭醴成婦禮也舅
姑入室婦以特豚饋明婦順也厥明舅姑
共饗婦以一獻之禮舅姑先降自西階婦
降自阼階以著代也義固各有當矣執事
所謂疑於奠酬未詳者盖禮有姑薦婦酢
舅更爵自薦之文賈疏謂舅獻姑酬共成
一獻則是舅洗于南洗而酌于阼以獻婦
婦易爵以酢舅既則姑洗於北洗酌以酬
===
婦婦奠于薦左而禮備矣此石梁王氏所
疑者其或然歟三月廟見三月然後執婦
功未三月則未成其為婦也此摻摻女手
可以縫裳見刺於魏風而廟見之詞所以
稱某氏來婦也今之昏禮行於縉紳或不
免因陋就簡罔知古人慎重之義而況於
齊民乎夫禮有
今制可遵矣苟考古而復得其意則廟見之
期與奠酬之節雖勿泥焉而固有所當重
punctuated: 見婦於舅姑，婦執笲棗栗腶脩，升自西階以見。贊醴婦，婦祭脯醢、祭醴，成婦禮也。舅姑入室，婦以特豚饋，明婦順也。厥明，舅姑共饗婦以一獻之禮，舅姑先降自西階，婦降自阼階，以著代也。義固各有當矣。執事所謂疑於奠酬未詳者，盖禮有姑薦、婦酢舅、更爵自薦之文。賈疏謂舅獻姑酬，共成一獻，則是舅洗于南洗，而酌于阼以獻婦，婦易爵以酢舅；既則姑洗於北洗，酌以酬婦，婦奠于薦左，而禮備矣。此石梁王氏所疑者，其或然歟？三月廟見，三月然後執婦功，未三月則未成其為婦也。此「摻摻女手，可以縫裳」見刺於《魏風》，而廟見之詞所以稱「某氏來婦」也。今之昏禮，行於縉紳，或不免因陋就簡，罔知古人慎重之義，而況於齊民乎？夫禮有今制可遵矣。苟考古而復得其意，則廟見之期與奠酬之節，雖勿泥焉，而固有所當重
translation_en:
…presents the bride to her parents-in-law. The bride carries baskets containing dates, chestnuts, and prepared dried meat, and ascends the western steps to meet them. The ritual assistant serves the bride sweet liquor; she makes offerings of dried meat and meat paste, and of sweet liquor. This completes the rite establishing her as a wife. Her parents-in-law enter the chamber, and she serves them a single piglet, demonstrating her obedience as a daughter-in-law. The following morning, her parents-in-law jointly entertain her with the rite of a single presentation of wine. They descend first by the western steps, while she descends by the eastern, host’s steps, making clear her succession to the household role. Each observance certainly has its appropriate meaning.

As for the uncertainty you express concerning the setting down of the cup and the pledging toast, the ritual text contains passages stating that the mother-in-law presents food, that the bride returns a toast to her father-in-law, and that he changes cups and presents food himself. Jia’s subcommentary says that the father-in-law makes the presentation of wine and the mother-in-law offers the pledging toast, together completing the rite of a single presentation. Thus the father-in-law washes a cup at the southern washing stand and pours wine at the eastern steps to present to the bride. She changes cups to return a toast to him. The mother-in-law then washes a cup at the northern washing stand and pours wine to offer the bride a pledging toast. The bride sets it down to the left of the food offerings, and the rite is complete. Might this be the explanation of the point questioned by Master Wang of Shiliang?

The bride is presented at the ancestral temple after three months, and only after three months does she undertake a wife’s work. Before those three months have passed, her standing as a wife is not yet complete. This is why the lines “Your slender hands can sew garments” occur as a criticism in the Airs of Wei, and why the formula for her presentation at the ancestral temple says, “A woman of such-and-such a clan has come to be a wife.” Wedding rites as now practiced among the gentry sometimes lapse into makeshift simplicity, without any understanding of the care and gravity intended by the ancients. How much more must this be so among the common people! For ritual, there are present regulations that may be followed. If one examines antiquity and recovers its underlying intent, then, although one need not adhere rigidly to the timing of the ancestral-temple presentation or the details of setting down the cup and offering the pledging toast, there are certainly matters to which due weight must be given…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
者矣鄉飲酒禮載於經而記有鄉飲酒義
合而考之賔祭脯醢祭酒敬禮也絕祭而
嚌肺嘗禮也啐酒成禮也介辭洗如賔而
不拜洗殺於賔也不嚌肺不啐酒不告旨
下賔也義固各有在矣然執事所謂賔主
介遵衆賔之位盖鄭註賔席牖前南面主
人席阼階上西面介席西階上東面席衆
賔於賔席之西席遵席於賔東盖即記之
所謂坐賔於西北坐介於西南以輔賔主
===
人位於東南坐僎於東北以輔主所謂賔
必南向介必東向主人必居東方者亦既
合矣為是舉者非職為興賢獻于王鄉故
鄉大夫為主賢者及其次為介為衆賔公
若大夫自外來觀禮者則為遵盖此專主
於賔賢而正齒位之說不與焉今之鄉飲
舉於有司則職為齒德而主介位皆北向
有可考者或乃以隅坐為位豈於禮若圖
未之考邪夫禮有
punctuated: 者矣。鄉飲酒禮載於經，而記有《鄉飲酒義》，合而考之：賔祭脯醢、祭酒，敬禮也；絕祭而嚌肺，嘗禮也；啐酒，成禮也。介辭洗如賔，而不拜洗，殺於賔也；不嚌肺，不啐酒，不告旨，下賔也。義固各有在矣。然執事所謂賔、主、介、遵、衆賔之位，盖鄭註：賔席牖前，南面；主人席阼階上，西面；介席西階上，東面；席衆賔於賔席之西；席遵，席於賔東。盖即記之所謂坐賔於西北，坐介於西南以輔賔，主人位於東南，坐僎於東北以輔主。所謂賔必南向、介必東向、主人必居東方者，亦既合矣。為是舉者，非職為興賢獻于王鄉？故鄉大夫為主，賢者及其次為介、為衆賔。公若大夫自外來觀禮者，則為遵。盖此專主於賔賢，而正齒位之說不與焉。今之鄉飲舉於有司，則職為齒德，而主、介位皆北向。有可考者，或乃以隅坐為位，豈於禮若圖未之考邪？夫禮有
translation_en:
…there are indeed matters that ought to be given weight. The district drinking ceremony is recorded in the classic, while the Record of Rites contains “The Meaning of the District Drinking Ceremony.” Examining them together, we find that the principal guest’s offerings of dried meat, meat sauce, and wine express reverence for the rite; breaking off an offering and tasting the lung constitute the ritual tasting; and sipping the wine completes the rite. The assistant guest declines the washing of the cup just as the principal guest does, but does not bow in acknowledgment of the washing: his ceremonial honors are less than those of the principal guest. He neither tastes the lung nor sips the wine nor declares its excellence: his standing is below that of the principal guest. Each practice certainly has its own significance.
As for the positions of the principal guest, host, assistant guest, honored visitor, and assembled guests mentioned by Your Honor, Zheng’s commentary explains: the principal guest’s mat is before the window, facing south; the host’s mat is above the eastern steps, facing west; the assistant guest’s mat is above the western steps, facing east; the assembled guests are seated west of the principal guest’s mat; and the honored visitor is seated east of it. This corresponds to what the Record says: seat the principal guest in the northwest and the assistant guest in the southwest to assist him; place the host in the southeast and seat the honored visitor in the northeast to assist him. Thus the statements that the principal guest must face south, the assistant guest must face east, and the host must occupy the eastern side are also consistent.
Was not the specific purpose of holding this ceremony to promote worthy men and present them to the king [?]? Hence the district grand master serves as host, while the worthy men and those next in standing serve as assistant guest and assembled guests [?]. A duke or grand master coming from elsewhere to observe the rite serves as honored visitor. This ceremony is thus devoted specifically to honoring worthy men as guests; the principle of arranging seats according to age does not enter into it.
The district drinking ceremony now conducted by the responsible authorities is specifically concerned with age and virtue, and the host and assistant guest both face north. There are sources by which this can be investigated, yet some assign seats at the corners. Can it be that they have not examined the ritual text and its diagrams? Now, as for ritual, there are…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
今制可遵矣苟考古而復得其意則情文兼
至化行俗美而古昔賓興之舉與位序文
節雖稍異焉而固有相協者矣是則覲禮
受於廟則祖考重祭禮行於旅酬則兄弟
洽昏禮著代則父子冢庶之分明鄉飲酒
和樂不流則朋友萃聚之道正夫覲禮固
不專主於嚴君臣也祭禮固不專主於明
父子也昏固不專主於重夫婦也鄉飲酒
固不專主於明長幼也此誠所謂禮之大
體聖人因人情而節文之于以明人倫厚
===
風俗僅見於遺經幸有傳於今者也愚雖
不敏敢不求益聞所未聞以無失古人之
意無昧
今日之制無愧於世之通儒則執事之盛心
亦可以無負矣
第四問
王九疇
同考試官教授劉 批〔用刑為治所不免然關係〕
punctuated:
今制可遵矣。苟考古而復得其意，則情文兼至，化行俗美，而古昔賓興之舉與位序文節雖稍異焉，而固有相協者矣。是則覲禮受於廟，則祖考重；祭禮行於旅酬，則兄弟洽；昏禮著代，則父子冢庶之分明；鄉飲酒和樂不流，則朋友萃聚之道正。夫覲禮固不專主於嚴君臣也，祭禮固不專主於明父子也，昏固不專主於重夫婦也，鄉飲酒固不專主於明長幼也。此誠所謂禮之大體，聖人因人情而節文之，于以明人倫、厚風俗，僅見於遺經，幸有傳於今者也。愚雖不敏，敢不求益，聞所未聞，以無失古人之意，無昧今日之制，無愧於世之通儒，則執事之盛心亦可以無負矣。

第四問
王九疇
同考試官教授劉 批〔用刑為治所不免，然關係〕
translation_en:
…there are present regulations to follow. If, by examining antiquity, we also recover their underlying intent, then both feeling and outward form will be fully realized, moral transformation will take effect, and customs will improve. Although the ancient practice of ceremonially honoring and recommending worthy men differed somewhat in its arrangement of places and ceremonial forms, there are nevertheless points of agreement.

Thus, when the audience rite is received in the ancestral temple, ancestors are honored; when sacrificial rites proceed to the general exchange of toasts, brothers are brought into harmony; when marriage rites make succession manifest, the distinctions between father and son and between the principal heir and the other sons become clear; and when the district drinking ceremony is harmonious and joyful without excess, the proper way for friends to gather is established. The audience rite is certainly not concerned solely with maintaining strict relations between ruler and minister; sacrificial rites are certainly not concerned solely with clarifying relations between father and son; marriage is certainly not concerned solely with giving weight to relations between husband and wife; and the district drinking ceremony is certainly not concerned solely with clarifying relations between senior and junior. This is truly what is called the essential substance of ritual: the sages followed human feelings and gave them measured, patterned expression, thereby clarifying human relationships and enriching customs. This can be seen only in the surviving classics, which fortunately have been transmitted to the present.

Though I am untalented, dare I fail to seek further instruction and hear what I have not yet heard, so as neither to lose the intent of the ancients nor to remain ignorant of present regulations, and to have no cause for shame before the learned scholars of our age? Then I may also avoid disappointing your generous intentions.

Fourth Policy Question
Wang Jiuchou 王九疇
Associate Examiner Liu 劉, Confucian School Professor, comments: 〔The use of punishments is unavoidable in governing, yet it concerns…〕

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
民命匪輕此策敷答貫徹古今其有志用世者歟錄之
考試官主事陳　批〔用刑以平字立論最是〕
考試官右給事中劉　批〔得明刑弼教之意〕
有育天下之仁有正天下之義曷為仁德
化是也曷為義刑罰是也一於仁而不斷
之以義則民知愛之而不知畏其弊流為
姑息而無以立精明之治一於義而不施
之以仁則民知畏之而不知愛其弊流為
殘忍而有以虧渾厚之體惟夫仁義並行
===
恩威兼濟而天下始無偏而不舉之弊矣
執事發策而以刑之寬嚴下詢愚以為一
於寬固不可也一於嚴亦不可也惟得其
平而已矣得其平斯得其情而民協于中
矣且聖人豈樂於用刑哉不得已也如天
之於萬物也煦之以陽和而必繼之以肅
殺蓋翕聚之不深則發散之不廣而天地
之化或幾乎息矣聖人之於民也本之以
德化而必輔之以刑罰蓋約束之不嚴則
punctuated:
民命匪輕，此策敷答，貫徹古今，其有志用世者歟？錄之。
考試官主事陳　批〔用刑以平字立論，最是。〕
考試官右給事中劉　批〔得明刑弼教之意。〕
有育天下之仁，有正天下之義。曷為仁？德化是也。曷為義？刑罰是也。一於仁而不斷之以義，則民知愛之而不知畏，其弊流為姑息，而無以立精明之治；一於義而不施之以仁，則民知畏之而不知愛，其弊流為殘忍，而有以虧渾厚之體。惟夫仁義並行，恩威兼濟，而天下始無偏而不舉之弊矣。
執事發策，而以刑之寬嚴下詢，愚以為一於寬，固不可也；一於嚴，亦不可也。惟得其平而已矣。得其平，斯得其情，而民協于中矣。且聖人豈樂於用刑哉？不得已也。如天之於萬物也，煦之以陽和，而必繼之以肅殺。蓋翕聚之不深，則發散之不廣，而天地之化或幾乎息矣。聖人之於民也，本之以德化，而必輔之以刑罰。蓋約束之不嚴，則
translation_en:
…the lives of the people are no trifling matter. This policy essay develops its answer comprehensively, encompassing past and present. Surely its author aspires to serve the world? Include it in the record.
Examiner Chen, Bureau Secretary, comments: 〔It is entirely right to ground the discussion of punishment in the word “equity.”〕
Examiner Liu, Supervising Secretary of the Right, comments: 〔It grasps the meaning of making punishments clear to support moral instruction.〕
There is benevolence that nurtures all under Heaven, and righteousness that sets all under Heaven right. What constitutes benevolence? Transformation through virtue. What constitutes righteousness? Punishments. If one relies exclusively on benevolence without making judgments through righteousness, the people will know affection but not fear. The resulting abuse degenerates into indulgence, leaving no means to establish discerning government. If one relies exclusively on righteousness without administering it through benevolence, the people will know fear but not affection. The resulting abuse degenerates into cruelty, impairing the substance of generous and substantial government. Only when benevolence and righteousness operate together, and favor and authority complement each other, will all under Heaven be free of the failings that arise when partiality leaves some matters unattended.
You, honored examiners, have set a policy question and deigned to ask about leniency and severity in punishment. In my humble view, exclusive reliance on leniency is certainly unacceptable; exclusive reliance on severity is likewise unacceptable. One must simply attain equity. When equity is attained, the true circumstances of each case are understood, and the people accord with the mean. Moreover, could the sage delight in using punishments? He has no alternative. It is like Heaven’s treatment of the myriad things: it warms them with the genial force of yang, yet must follow this with stern, killing cold. For unless gathering and storing are deep, unfolding and dispersal cannot be extensive, and the transforming activity of Heaven and Earth might almost cease. In dealing with the people, the sage takes transformation through virtue as his foundation, yet must supplement it with punishments. For if restraints are not strict, then…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
聲教之或梗而聖人之化於是乎窮矣是
則刑者聖人之所不廢也故曰殺人以安
人殺之可也聖人之用刑豈得已哉舜典
曰象以典刑流宥五刑鞭作官刑扑作教
刑金作贖刑禹謨曰宥過無大刑故無小
周禮秋官司寇掌邦禁以佐王刑邦國又
曰以五刑糾萬民由此觀之則唐虞三代
之治雖未嘗專於用刑而未嘗不以刑爲
之輔也周穆王作呂刑五刑之疑有赦五
===
罰之疑有赦今讀其書猶可想見三代忠
厚之遺意而蔡氏作傳乃病其大辟亦與
贖免故以爲穆王巡遊無度財匱民勞爲
此一切權宜之術以歛民財固也而馬端
臨又謂其罪之疑者不遽赦之而姑取其
鍰以示罰非利其貨也斯言豈無所見乎
然上刑適輕下服何必以贖爲哉漢文帝
除肉刑曰死者不可復生斷者不可復續
令誦其言真足以見仁人君子之用心歟
punctuated: 聲教之或梗，而聖人之化於是乎窮矣。是則刑者，聖人之所不廢也。故曰：「殺人以安人，殺之可也。」聖人之用刑，豈得已哉？《舜典》曰：「象以典刑，流宥五刑，鞭作官刑，扑作教刑，金作贖刑。」《禹謨》曰：「宥過無大，刑故無小。」《周禮》秋官司寇掌邦禁，以佐王刑邦國，又曰：「以五刑糾萬民。」由此觀之，則唐虞三代之治，雖未嘗專於用刑，而未嘗不以刑爲之輔也。周穆王作《呂刑》：「五刑之疑有赦，五罰之疑有赦。」今讀其書，猶可想見三代忠厚之遺意。而蔡氏作傳，乃病其大辟亦與贖免，故以爲穆王巡遊無度，財匱民勞，爲此一切權宜之術，以歛民財，固也。而馬端臨又謂其罪之疑者，不遽赦之，而姑取其鍰以示罰，非利其貨也。斯言豈無所見乎？然「上刑適輕，下服」，何必以贖爲哉？漢文帝除肉刑，曰：「死者不可復生，斷者不可復續。」令誦其言，真足以見仁人君子之用心歟？
translation_en:
…the civilizing influence of their teachings may be obstructed, and the transforming power of the sages will thereby reach its limit. Punishment, then, is something the sages do not dispense with. Thus it is said: “If killing someone brings peace to others, it is permissible to kill him.” Could the sages’ use of punishment be anything but a necessity? The Canon of Shun states: “Set forth the regular punishments; use exile to mitigate the five punishments; employ whipping as punishment for officials, beating as punishment in instruction, and payments in metal to redeem punishments.” The Counsels of Yu states: “Pardon inadvertent offenses, however great; punish deliberate offenses, however small.” In the Rites of Zhou, the Minister of Justice, head of the Ministry of Autumn, administers the prohibitions of the realm to assist the king in applying penal law to the states. It also says: “Correct the myriad people through the five punishments.” Seen in this light, although the governments of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties never relied exclusively on punishment, they invariably used it as an aid.

King Mu of Zhou composed the Punishments of Lü: “Where there is doubt concerning the five punishments, there is remission; where there is doubt concerning the five fines, there is remission.” Reading this text today, one can still envisage the surviving spirit of loyalty and generosity of the Three Dynasties. Yet Master Cai, in writing his commentary, objected that even capital punishment could be remitted through payment. He therefore held that King Mu, whose excursions knew no bounds and had exhausted the treasury and wearied the people, devised these expedients to extract the people’s wealth. This is certainly a sound argument. Ma Duanlin, however, maintained that, where guilt was doubtful, the authorities did not immediately grant a pardon but provisionally exacted a fine in metal to signify punishment; they were not seeking profit from the offenders’ wealth. Surely this statement reflects some insight? Nevertheless, “When an offense assigned a heavier punishment warrants leniency, impose the next lighter punishment.” Why, then, was redemption by payment necessary?

Emperor Wen of Han abolished mutilating punishments, saying: “The dead cannot be restored to life, and severed limbs cannot be rejoined.” Reciting his words [?], can one not truly perceive the intentions of a benevolent man and gentleman?

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
後崔寔著政論乃謂文帝雖除肉刑當劓
者笞三百當斬左趾笞五百當斬右趾者
棄市右趾者既殞其命笞撻者往往至死
雖有輕刑之名其實殺也又曰文帝乃重
刑非輕之也以嚴致平非以寬致平也寔
蓋痛漢季之不振而為是論其言豈有所
激乎然刑罰世重世輕何必泥於古哉洪
惟我
聖祖承胡元亂華之後憫綱常倫理之斁於是
===
嚴法以治之一洗腥羶之俗以回淳古之
風乃命刑部尚書劉惟謙等取前代諸律
斟酌損益而又
親灑宸翰為之裁定
大明律一書上稽天理下合人心真百王之
大法萬世之準繩自有法律以來未之有
也又慮後世或有流於嚴者故載諸
祖訓條章諄諄以輕於用刑為戒又因刑部奏
決重刑
punctuated:
後崔寔著《政論》，乃謂文帝雖除肉刑，當劓者笞三百，當斬左趾笞五百，當斬右趾者棄市。右趾者既殞其命，笞撻者往往至死，雖有輕刑之名，其實殺也。又曰：「文帝乃重刑，非輕之也；以嚴致平，非以寬致平也。」寔蓋痛漢季之不振而為是論，其言豈有所激乎？然刑罰世重世輕，何必泥於古哉？
洪惟我聖祖承胡元亂華之後，憫綱常倫理之斁，於是嚴法以治之，一洗腥羶之俗，以回淳古之風。乃命刑部尚書劉惟謙等取前代諸律，斟酌損益，而又親灑宸翰，為之裁定。《大明律》一書，上稽天理，下合人心，真百王之大法、萬世之準繩，自有法律以來未之有也。又慮後世或有流於嚴者，故載諸《祖訓》條章，諄諄以輕於用刑為戒。又因刑部奏決重刑
translation_en:
Later, Cui Shi wrote his Discourse on Government (Zhenglun), in which he argued that although Emperor Wen abolished mutilating punishments, those liable to have their noses cut off received three hundred strokes, those liable to lose their left foot received five hundred strokes, and those liable to lose their right foot were executed in the marketplace. Those sentenced to lose their right foot thus forfeited their lives, while those subjected to flogging frequently died. Although this bore the name of mitigating punishment, in reality it meant killing. He further said: “Emperor Wen made punishments heavier, not lighter. He achieved peace through severity, not through leniency.” Cui Shi presumably advanced this argument out of distress at the decline of the late Han. Might his words have been provoked by particular circumstances? Yet punishments are heavier or lighter according to the age: why must one adhere rigidly to antiquity?
We reverently reflect that our sagely founder succeeded to rule after the barbarian Yuan had thrown China into disorder. Grieved by the corruption of the cardinal bonds, constant virtues, and ethical relationships, he governed with strict laws, sweeping away the rank and mutton-reeking customs to restore the pure ways of antiquity. He then ordered Liu Weiqian, Minister of Justice, and others to take the legal codes of previous dynasties and weigh what should be removed or added. He also personally wielded the imperial brush to revise and settle the text. The resulting Great Ming Code (Da Ming lü) accords above with heavenly principle and below with human hearts. Truly it is the great law for a hundred kings and the standard for ten thousand generations; nothing like it had existed since laws first came into being. He further feared that later generations might tend toward excessive severity. He therefore incorporated provisions into the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun), repeatedly warning against resorting lightly to punishment. Then, on another occasion, when the Ministry of Justice submitted a memorial requesting the carrying out of severe punishments…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
諭曰朕嘗命汝等凡有重獄必三覆奏自今
凡十惡非常赦所原者則云重刑其餘雜
犯死罪許聽收贖毋槩言也大哉
王言真仁人之言也聖人不得已而用刑之心
也
列聖相承行之百六十餘年而天下人心翕然
以定我
皇上以好生為德慎重民命屢
詔䘏刑中外百司奉行惟謹然猶未底刑措之
效者豈奉行者或有未至乎抑亦承平日
===
久而
祖宗之法或有未盡舉者乎夫簡細故以自崇
則獄有淹滯作聰明以自用則刑有出入
或褊急以遂其怒或慘刻以濟其欲而民
有斃於箠楚之下者矣或一人而連數十
人或一事而逮數處而民多陷於法網之
內者矣此所以厪我
皇上之慮而書所謂欽哉欽哉惟刑之䘏者吾
punctuated:
諭曰：「朕嘗命汝等，凡有重獄，必三覆奏。自今，凡十惡非常赦所原者，則云重刑；其餘雜犯死罪，許聽收贖，毋槩言也。」大哉，王言！真仁人之言也，聖人不得已而用刑之心也。
列聖相承，行之百六十餘年，而天下人心翕然以定。我皇上以好生為德，慎重民命，屢詔䘏刑，中外百司奉行惟謹。然猶未底刑措之效者，豈奉行者或有未至乎？抑亦承平日久，而祖宗之法或有未盡舉者乎？夫簡細故以自崇，則獄有淹滯；作聰明以自用，則刑有出入。或褊急以遂其怒，或慘刻以濟其欲，而民有斃於箠楚之下者矣；或一人而連數十人，或一事而逮數處，而民多陷於法網之內者矣。此所以厪我皇上之慮，而《書》所謂「欽哉，欽哉，惟刑之䘏」者，吾
translation_en:
…he issued an instruction, saying: “I previously commanded you that every serious criminal case must be submitted to me three times for review. Henceforth, only cases involving the Ten Abominations, which ordinary amnesties do not pardon, are to be described as ‘grave punishments.’ Those guilty of other miscellaneous capital offenses may be permitted to redeem their punishment by payment. Do not speak of them all indiscriminately.” How great are these royal words! They are truly the words of a humane man, expressing the sage’s resolve to employ punishment only when no other course remains.
Successive sage emperors continued this practice for more than 160 years, and the hearts of people throughout the realm were united and settled. Our Emperor cherishes life as a virtue and treats the lives of his people with utmost care. He has repeatedly issued edicts urging compassion in punishment, and the officials of all offices, both at court and in the provinces, have carried them out most diligently. Yet the result—punishments being set aside because they are no longer needed—has still not been attained. Could some of those charged with implementation have fallen short? Or, after so many years of peace, might some of the ancestral laws no longer be fully put into effect?
When officials dismiss minor matters to magnify their own importance, cases languish unresolved; when they parade their cleverness and act on their own judgment, punishments are improperly reduced or increased. Some give vent to their anger through impatience and narrow-mindedness; others gratify their desires through cruelty, so that people die beneath the rods. Sometimes one person implicates dozens of others, or one affair brings arrests in several places, so that many people become ensnared in the net of the law. This is what burdens our Emperor with concern. As for the words of the Book of Documents, “Be reverent! Be reverent! Give compassionate care to punishment,” we …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
在位所宜究心也宋儒朱子嘗有論著大
約謂三綱五常治道之本根教以明之而
後刑以弼之又謂鄙儒姑息之論俗吏便
文之計一以輕刑為事刑愈輕而愈不足
以厚民之俗蓋一則言刑之施必先事乎
教而不可以徒用一則言刑之卹惟在得
其平而不專在於寬此即古聖人卹刑之
意也今日
祖宗之法具在惟在奉行者執之而已法所不
===
宥雖貴近而必先罪所當原雖幽隱而必
察殺人之囚必與衆棄之而不使其遷延
以庾死貪墨之吏必明正其罪而不使其
僥倖以苟容則刑得其平而人心自無不
和刑罰中而禮樂可興矣或乃謂今之人
心漸不如古故刑不勝奸愚則以為天理
之在人心固未嘗泯也雖然愚又有說焉
記曰刑者成也一成而不可變者也是以
君子盡心焉書曰與其殺不辜寧失不經
punctuated:
在位所宜究心也。宋儒朱子嘗有論著，大約謂三綱五常，治道之本根，教以明之，而後刑以弼之。又謂鄙儒姑息之論、俗吏便文之計，一以輕刑為事，刑愈輕而愈不足以厚民之俗。蓋一則言刑之施必先事乎教，而不可以徒用；一則言刑之卹惟在得其平，而不專在於寬。此即古聖人卹刑之意也。
今日祖宗之法具在，惟在奉行者執之而已。法所不宥，雖貴近而必先；罪所當原，雖幽隱而必察。殺人之囚，必與衆棄之，而不使其遷延以庾死；貪墨之吏，必明正其罪，而不使其僥倖以苟容。則刑得其平，而人心自無不和；刑罰中，而禮樂可興矣。或乃謂今之人心漸不如古，故刑不勝奸。愚則以為天理之在人心，固未嘗泯也。
雖然，愚又有說焉。《記》曰：「刑者，成也；一成而不可變者也，是以君子盡心焉。」《書》曰：「與其殺不辜，寧失不經。」
translation_en:
…is what those of us holding office ought to consider deeply. The Song Confucian scholar Master Zhu once wrote on this subject. His general argument was that the Three Bonds and Five Constants are the foundations of good government: education makes them clear, and punishments then support them. He also argued that the indulgent doctrines of shallow scholars and the expedient schemes of commonplace officials, concerned only with satisfying the letter of the law, make light punishments their sole objective. Yet the lighter the punishments become, the less adequate they are to make the people's customs sound. The first argument means that education must precede the application of punishments, which cannot be employed alone; the second means that solicitude in punishment consists in achieving equity, rather than exclusively in leniency. This is precisely what the ancient sages intended by solicitude in punishment.
Today the laws of our imperial ancestors remain fully in place; all depends upon those charged with implementing them upholding them. Where the law permits no pardon, even the eminent and those close to the throne must be dealt with first. Where an offense merits forgiveness, even the cases of the obscure and unnoticed must be investigated. Those imprisoned for murder must be put to death in accordance with the judgment of the community, rather than allowed to linger and die in confinement [?]. Corrupt officials must have their offenses openly adjudicated and punished, rather than be allowed to escape by good fortune and remain in office through improper indulgence. Then punishments will be equitable, and people's hearts will naturally be harmonious. When punishments are fitting, rites and music can flourish. Some say that people's hearts today have gradually fallen below those of antiquity, and that this is why punishments cannot overcome wrongdoing. In my humble view, however, heavenly principle has never been extinguished in people's hearts.
Nevertheless, I have something further to say. The Book of Rites states: “Punishment means completion: once completed, it cannot be altered. Therefore the gentleman devotes his utmost care to it.” The Book of Documents states: “Rather than kill an innocent person, it is preferable to err by departing from the established rule.”

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
君子之治刑也虛心平氣以竟其辭不使
一毫喜怒橫之於中一念利害怵之于外
未有不得其平者也此執事所謂有德惟
刑哀敬折獄者而豈無其人哉然必好生
之德洽於民心使之有道教之有素俾自
不犯于有司不幸而有麗于刑者則如前
所謂盡心焉則德化施而仁足以育天下
刑罰用而義足以正天下庶乎民得其分
有司得其職而
===
聖朝制作之意庶可以不失
皇上好生之德庶可以少助而刑期無刑矣敢
以是為明問復
第五問
安宅
同考試官教諭胡　批　時務策非學識兼至
難於敷對子獨能援古論今區畫詳盡可以
占所養矣
考試官主事陳　批　策有識見殆有用之學
punctuated:
君子之治刑也，虛心平氣以竟其辭，不使一毫喜怒橫之於中，一念利害怵之于外，未有不得其平者也。此執事所謂有德惟刑、哀敬折獄者，而豈無其人哉？然必好生之德洽於民心，使之有道，教之有素，俾自不犯于有司。不幸而有麗于刑者，則如前所謂盡心焉，則德化施而仁足以育天下，刑罰用而義足以正天下。庶乎民得其分，有司得其職，而聖朝制作之意庶可以不失，皇上好生之德庶可以少助，而刑期無刑矣。敢以是為明問復。

第五問
安宅

同考試官教諭胡　批：時務策，非學識兼至，難於敷對。子獨能援古論今，區畫詳盡，可以占所養矣。

考試官主事陳　批：策有識見，殆有用之學
translation_en:
When a gentleman administers punishments, he clears his mind and calms his temper so as to hear the statements through to the end. He allows neither the slightest pleasure or anger to intrude within nor any thought of gain or loss to alarm him from without. In this way, he invariably achieves fairness. These are the men you refer to when you speak of exercising virtue in punishment and deciding cases with compassion and reverence. How could there be no such men?

Yet the virtue of cherishing life must thoroughly imbue the people’s hearts. They must be directed in the proper way and consistently instructed, so that they themselves avoid offending against the authorities. If any should unfortunately incur punishment, officials must devote their utmost care to the matter, as stated above. Then moral transformation will spread, and benevolence will suffice to nurture all under Heaven; punishments will be applied, and righteousness will suffice to set all under Heaven right. We may thus hope that the people will fulfill their proper roles and officials discharge their duties, that the intentions behind our sagely dynasty’s institutions will be preserved, and that His Majesty’s virtue of cherishing life will receive some small assistance. Punishment will then serve its ultimate purpose of eliminating the need for punishment. I venture to offer this in reply to your discerning question.

Fifth Question
An Zhai 安宅

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu 胡, Instructor: A policy essay on current affairs is difficult to expound unless both learning and discernment are fully developed. You alone have been able to draw on antiquity to discuss the present, setting out plans in exhaustive detail. From this one can judge the cultivation you have attained.

Comment by Examiner Chen 陳, Secretary: This policy essay displays discernment; surely its author possesses learning of practical use…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
者
考試官右給事中劉　批　〔明體達　用之學〕
善計國者必通天下之變而審其經焉天
下之變無窮也不視其緩急之勢變而通
之則無以妙達權救敝之宜天下之道有
常也不審乎一定之術執而守之則無以
立久安長治之法通變審經而天下無不
可為之事矣孰事以
國之重計下詢承學草茅賤士何足以知之
===
然明問所及敢不罄一得之愚以對方今
旱蝗荐作稼穡盡空盖生民之患也俯仰
無資勢將展轉為民父母而可無賑恤之
政乎發廩勸分徙民移粟弛力薄征酌而
行之其可也尤必因天變而交儆焉六事
自責如成湯之禱於桑林克正厥事如高
宗之聽於祖己戰兢惕厲于以敬天之怒
毋敢戲豫而馳驅則庶乎轉禍為福而災
害不生矣漕河淤淺疏鑿他道避黄河之
punctuated:
者。
考試官右給事中劉，批：〔明體達　用之學〕
善計國者，必通天下之變而審其經焉。天下之變無窮也，不視其緩急之勢，變而通之，則無以妙達權救敝之宜。天下之道有常也，不審乎一定之術，執而守之，則無以立久安長治之法。通變審經，而天下無不可為之事矣。孰事以國之重計，下詢承學草茅賤士，何足以知之？然明問所及，敢不罄一得之愚以對？方今旱蝗荐作，稼穡盡空，盖生民之患也。俯仰無資，勢將展轉，為民父母而可無賑恤之政乎？發廩勸分，徙民移粟，弛力薄征，酌而行之，其可也。尤必因天變而交儆焉。六事自責，如成湯之禱於桑林；克正厥事，如高宗之聽於祖己。戰兢惕厲，于以敬天之怒，毋敢戲豫而馳驅，則庶乎轉禍為福，而災害不生矣。漕河淤淺，疏鑿他道，避黄河之
translation_en:
…one possessed of such learning.
Examiner Liu, Right Supervising Secretary, comments: 〔Learning that comprehends fundamental principles and masters their practical application.〕
Those who plan well for the state must understand changing circumstances throughout the realm and carefully examine its enduring principles. Changes throughout the realm are inexhaustible. Unless one considers their relative urgency and adapts accordingly, one cannot exercise discretion with subtlety or find appropriate remedies for abuses. The Way governing the realm has its constants. Unless one carefully examines settled methods and holds firmly to them, one cannot establish measures for lasting peace and enduring good government. With an understanding of change and a careful examination of enduring principles, nothing in the realm is impossible to accomplish. You [?] have condescended to consult humble scholars outside official service about the state's weighty plans. How could we be adequate to understand them? Yet, concerning the matters raised in your discerning question, how could I dare not offer in reply the full extent of my limited understanding?
At present, droughts and locusts have repeatedly struck, leaving the harvest utterly barren: this is indeed a calamity for the people. With no means to support either their parents or their children, they will inevitably be driven to wander. Can those who act as the people's parents dispense with measures for relief? Opening granaries and encouraging the sharing of grain, relocating people and transporting grain, easing labor obligations and reducing levies—these may properly be implemented as circumstances warrant. Above all, Heaven's portents must prompt mutual admonition. One should reproach oneself on six counts, as Cheng Tang did when praying at Sanglin, and duly rectify one's conduct, as Gaozong did when heeding Zu Ji. Trembling, vigilant, and earnest, one should thus show reverence for Heaven's anger, daring neither to indulge in idle pleasures nor to gallop about in pursuit of amusement. Then perhaps calamity may be turned into blessing, and disasters will cease to arise. The grain-transport canal has silted up and become shallow; dredging and excavating another route would avoid the Yellow River's…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
患也然兩河之水勢必相通舊者既淤而
新者能保不淤乎新河縱避其淤瀕河居
民墊溺孰拯利國而病民不可也誠能因
其勢而利導之倣九河之遺意而分殺其
流修平江之舊法而稍藉其潤斟酌劑量
毋敢輕用民力特詘而舉羸則庶乎轉淤
為通而漕運有賴矣賦斂所以足軍需也
財貨所聚非官則民
國家取民既有定制而蠲免之
===
詔屢下宜其民之益富矣然閭閻之衆猶愁苦
而不蘇者執事所謂貪吏豪民之橐橐民
俗奢侈之害財信然矣誠使在上者嚴貪
饕之誅厲兼并之禁等威以辯而庶民不
得以僭公卿執物以明而娼優不得以擬
后飾則民財庶乎少省矣若探其本則必
去三冗而後可焉朝多倖位吏有剩員吏
之冗也養之徒以病農用之不能禦敵兵
之冗也或好興作或濫賞與費之冗也求
punctuated:
患也。然兩河之水勢必相通，舊者既淤，而新者能保不淤乎？新河縱避其淤，瀕河居民墊溺孰拯？利國而病民，不可也。誠能因其勢而利導之，倣九河之遺意而分殺其流，修平江之舊法而稍藉其潤，斟酌劑量，毋敢輕用民力，特詘而舉羸，則庶乎轉淤為通，而漕運有賴矣。
賦斂所以足軍需也。財貨所聚，非官則民。國家取民既有定制，而蠲免之詔屢下，宜其民之益富矣。然閭閻之衆猶愁苦而不蘇者，執事所謂貪吏豪民之橐橐、民俗奢侈之害財，信然矣。誠使在上者嚴貪饕之誅，厲兼并之禁，等威以辯，而庶民不得以僭公卿；執物以明，而娼優不得以擬后飾，則民財庶乎少省矣。若探其本，則必去三冗而後可焉。朝多倖位，吏有剩員，吏之冗也；養之徒以病農，用之不能禦敵，兵之冗也；或好興作，或濫賞與，費之冗也。求
translation_en:
…its dangers. Yet the waters of the two rivers must communicate with one another. If the old channel has silted up, can one guarantee that the new one will not? Even if the new river avoids silting, who will rescue the inhabitants along its banks from flooding and drowning? To benefit the state while harming the people is unacceptable. If we can guide the waters advantageously according to their natural course, follow the principle underlying the nine channels by dividing and reducing the flow, and restore the old methods of Pingjiang so as to draw some benefit from the water, carefully weighing and adjusting our measures and never rashly expending the people's labor, relieving hardship and supporting the weak [?], then we may hope to turn an obstructed channel into an open passage on which grain transport can depend.
Taxes and levies serve to meet military needs. Wealth accumulates either with the government or with the people. The state's exactions from the people already follow fixed regulations, and edicts granting tax remissions have repeatedly been issued; the people ought therefore to have become increasingly prosperous. Yet the common people remain distressed and have not recovered. What you have said about the grasping of corrupt officials and powerful commoners [?], and the depletion of wealth caused by extravagant popular habits, is indeed true. If those above strictly punish rapacity and enforce prohibitions against engrossment, clearly distinguish the degrees of rank so that commoners cannot usurp the privileges of dukes and high ministers, and make clear the rules governing articles appropriate to each station so that prostitutes and actors cannot imitate the empress's ornaments, then the people's wealth may be spared to some extent. But to reach the root of the matter, we must eliminate the three forms of redundancy. When the court has many who gain positions through favor, and official establishments have surplus personnel, this is redundancy among officials. When maintaining soldiers merely burdens the farmers, while employing them fails to repel the enemy, this is redundancy among troops. When some delight in launching construction projects and others bestow rewards indiscriminately, this is redundancy in expenditure. Seek out…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
其流而節之而又立歲會以考其成何患
民之不富而國用之不足哉盜賊迫於饑
寒也好生惡死人心所同
朝廷時見撫綏而征勦之兵四出宜其民之
自愛矣然潢池之兵猶盜弄而不息者執
事所謂有司撫馭之無方承平武備之不
振信然矣誠使在上者張皇義師擣其巢
穴渠魁盡誅而脅從使足以奪姦雄之氣
脅從姑置而不治又有以安反側之心則
===
盜賊庶乎可平矣若究其極則必塞三源
而後可焉衣食不足盜之源也賦役不均
盜之源也敎化不修盜之源也求其源而
止之而又修武備於未然何患民之不安
而盜之不弭哉大抵通變於先所以濟經
之不及審經於後所以復吾治之常然非
司
國計者參伍而錯綜之焉則天下之事日就
於弊而已矣狂瞽之言俾得上達以備
punctuated:
其流而節之，而又立歲會以考其成，何患民之不富而國用之不足哉？盜賊迫於饑寒也，好生惡死，人心所同。朝廷時見撫綏，而征勦之兵四出，宜其民之自愛矣。然潢池之兵猶盜弄而不息者，執事所謂有司撫馭之無方、承平武備之不振，信然矣。誠使在上者張皇義師，擣其巢穴，渠魁盡誅而脅從使足以奪姦雄之氣，脅從姑置而不治，又有以安反側之心，則盜賊庶乎可平矣。若究其極，則必塞三源而後可焉。衣食不足，盜之源也；賦役不均，盜之源也；敎化不修，盜之源也。求其源而止之，而又修武備於未然，何患民之不安而盜之不弭哉？
大抵通變於先，所以濟經之不及；審經於後，所以復吾治之常。然非司國計者參伍而錯綜之焉，則天下之事日就於弊而已矣。狂瞽之言，俾得上達，以備
translation_en:
…their outflows and curb them, and also establish annual accounts to assess the results: why then worry that the people will not prosper or that resources for state expenditure will be insufficient? Bandits are driven by hunger and cold. To cherish life and abhor death is common to all human hearts. The court repeatedly extends pacification and reassurance, while troops march out in all directions to suppress banditry; one would expect the people to cherish their own lives. Yet they still seize weapons and stir up petty rebellions without cease. Your observation that the responsible officials lack effective methods of pacification and control, and that military preparedness has languished in prolonged peace, is indeed correct. If those above would muster a righteous army and strike the bandits’ lairs, executing all the ringleaders—the passage concerning those coerced into following them is unclear [?]—this would suffice to break the resolve of the treacherous strongmen. If those coerced into joining were provisionally spared and not punished, this would also reassure those wavering in fear. Banditry might then be quelled. But to pursue the matter to its ultimate basis, its three sources must first be blocked. Inadequate food and clothing are a source of banditry; unequal taxation and labor service are a source of banditry; neglect of moral instruction is a source of banditry. Seek out these sources and stop them, and also strengthen military preparedness before trouble arises: why then worry that the people will not be secure or that banditry will not cease?
In general, adapting to change at the outset remedies what established principles cannot adequately address; examining those principles afterward restores the regular order of our government. Yet unless those responsible for state finances compare and cross-check these measures and coordinate them, the affairs of the realm will simply deteriorate day by day. May these rash and unenlightened words be conveyed to those above, to be available for …

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text: 采擇之萬一執事之賜也
punctuated: 采擇之萬一，執事之賜也。
translation_en: …so that even the smallest part might be considered for adoption: this would be a favor bestowed by you, honored officials.

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
嘉靖戊子秋八月寔惟賓興
之期右給事中劉世揚曁〔簏〕
被
命主山東試事自惟菲才大懼弗
稱晝夜校閱惟勤惟慎期得
真才以副
===
聖天子側席求賢之盛心者亦惟
盡厥心焉耳錄成簏當序諸
末簡竊惟治理資于人才而
人才學術有邪有正蓋自選
舉之法廢而科目興士之所
謂學術者率於文焉見之是
故學術醇正其爲文也必明
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

嘉靖戊子秋八月，寔惟賓興之期。右給事中劉世揚曁〔簏〕被命主山東試事，自惟菲才，大懼弗稱，晝夜校閱，惟勤惟慎，期得真才，以副聖天子側席求賢之盛心者，亦惟盡厥心焉耳。錄成，簏當序諸末簡。竊惟治理資于人才，而人才學術有邪有正。蓋自選舉之法廢而科目興，士之所謂學術者，率於文焉見之。是故學術醇正，其爲文也必明
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the wuzi year of Jiajing [1528], the time had come to honor and advance worthy men. Right Supervising Secretary Liu Shiyang and I, 〔Lu [?]〕, received orders to preside over the Shandong examination. Conscious of my meager abilities, I greatly feared that I would prove unequal to the charge. Day and night we reviewed the papers, exercising diligence and care, hoping to obtain men of genuine talent and thereby fulfill the sagely Son of Heaven’s ardent desire to seek worthy men, for whom he leaves a place beside him. We could only devote ourselves wholeheartedly to this task. When the record was completed, it fell to me, Lu [?], to write a postface on its final leaves.

I humbly consider that good government depends upon talented men, but that their learning may be either misguided or correct. Since the methods of selection and recommendation were abandoned and the examination system arose, what is called a scholar’s learning has generally manifested itself in his writing. Thus, when his learning is pure and correct, his writing must be clear…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
白正大根極理道而見于功
業亦必磊磊落落俊偉光明
有足觀者矣其不然者反是
古所謂名世之臣臯夔伊傅
周召不可尚已今即其文觀
之如臯陶謨伊訓說命諸篇
有不明白正大根極理道者
===
乎謂文不足以觀人吾不信
也今諸士之文亦旣斐然矣
要之能以理勝者所謂學術
之正蓋於是乎見矣當今孔
孟之道如日中天海內之士
類能誦說而有所得況士之
產于其鄉而浸潤涵濡之久
punctuated: 白正大，根極理道，而見于功業，亦必磊磊落落，俊偉光明，有足觀者矣。其不然者反是。古所謂名世之臣，臯、夔、伊、傅、周、召，不可尚已。今即其文觀之，如《臯陶謨》《伊訓》《說命》諸篇，有不明白正大、根極理道者乎？謂文不足以觀人，吾不信也。今諸士之文亦旣斐然矣。要之，能以理勝者，所謂學術之正，蓋於是乎見矣。當今孔孟之道如日中天，海內之士類能誦說而有所得，況士之產于其鄉而浸潤涵濡之久
translation_en: …clear, upright, and broad in spirit, rooted ultimately in principle and the Way; when manifested in achievements, it must likewise be open and unreserved, outstanding and luminous, with much worthy of admiration. Those for whom this is not so display the opposite. The ministers of old renowned in their ages—Gao Yao, Kui, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao—cannot be surpassed. Now, if we examine their writings, such as the chapters “Counsels of Gao Yao,” “Instructions of Yi,” and “Charge to Yue,” is there any that is not clear, upright, and broad in spirit, rooted ultimately in principle and the Way? I do not believe the claim that writing is insufficient for judging a person. The writings of these gentlemen are already distinguished in literary accomplishment. In essence, where principle gives their writing its strength, what is called rectitude in learning is revealed. Today the Way of Kongzi and Mengzi is like the sun at its zenith. Scholars throughout the realm can generally recite and expound it and have gained some understanding of it. How much more, then, those scholars born in their native region, who have long been steeped and nurtured in their teachings…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
其所得顧不有倍焉者乎蓋
簾嘗竊料之矣以今觀之諒
哉諸士既以文錄于有司行
且試春官對
大廷有服百僚人將於子乎觀
政政與學非二也有孔孟之
學術而後有臯夔伊傅周召
之功業故曰或源也或委也
===
抑孰非儒者分內事哉彼誘
以不能焉者其自待也不已
薄乎如其靜言庸違家脩而
庭壞是又藉是以邀利祿者
爾豈
聖代設科求士之初意而產於聖
punctuated:
其所得顧不有倍焉者乎？蓋簾嘗竊料之矣，以今觀之，諒哉！諸士既以文錄于有司，行且試春官，對大廷，有服百僚，人將於子乎觀政。政與學非二也，有孔孟之學術，而後有臯夔伊傅周召之功業。故曰：或源也，或委也。
抑孰非儒者分內事哉？彼誘以不能焉者，其自待也不已薄乎？如其靜言庸違，家脩而庭壞，是又藉是以邀利祿者爾，豈聖代設科求士之初意？而產於聖
translation_en:
…would not what they have gained be greater still? I [?; the transcription reads 簾] had privately anticipated this; judging by what I now see, it is indeed so! You gentlemen have already been selected by the responsible officials on the strength of your compositions. Soon you will sit the examination at the Ministry of Rites, answer questions at the imperial court, and serve among the officials. People will then look to you to observe the conduct of government. Governing and learning are not two separate things. Only with the learning of Kongzi and Mengzi can one achieve the accomplishments of Gao Yao, Kui, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao. Thus it is said: one is the source, the other its downstream flow.
Indeed, which of these lies outside a Confucian scholar’s proper duties? Those who persuade themselves that they are incapable of this—do they not hold themselves in excessively low esteem? If, however, their quiet professions are contradicted by their conduct, and they cultivate themselves at home but fall into corruption at court, then they merely use this learning to seek profit and official emoluments. Could this be the original intention of our sagely dynasty in establishing examinations to seek worthy men? And those born in the homeland of the sages…

title: 嘉靖七年山東鄉試錄
text:
賢之鄉者亦豈宜有是哉麓
承之考校與有以人事
君之責者敢僭以是說爲告惟爾
諸士其尚懋戒之哉
刑部雲南清吏司主事陳麓
謹序
punctuated:
賢之鄉者，亦豈宜有是哉？麓承之考校，與有以人事君之責者，敢僭以是說爲告。惟爾諸士，其尚懋戒之哉！
刑部雲南清吏司主事陳麓謹序。
translation_en:
…the homeland of sages and worthies—how could such conduct be fitting for those born there either? I, Lu, having undertaken the work of examining [?], together with those responsible for serving the ruler by selecting men, venture presumptuously to offer these words of admonition. May you gentlemen earnestly heed this warning!
Preface respectfully composed by Chen Lu, Secretary in the Yunnan Bureau of the Ministry of Justice.
